column1: # Phase B round ledger — which axis each round advanced.
# Why this file exists (R1526). `tools/phase_b_tally.py` measures an axis by
# COUNTING artifacts, so it can only register work that CREATES one. Depth work
# modifies what already exists: R1523, R1524 and R1525 each closed a named gap
# in the Model/View contract by editing `hello-grid-*` examples the axis already
# owned, and the axis's evidence moved by +0%, +0%, +0%. R1520 and R1521 had
# done the same to the performance axis two rounds earlier. R1522 fixed that one
# by giving perf a `demo-body` probe, which worked only because an optimisation
# happens to leave a NEW demo behind — the cardinality blindness underneath was
# untouched, and it resurfaced on the next axis three rounds later.
# R1522 also recorded why the tool cannot infer this: "a demo is named for the
# round it served and EVERY round has one whatever axis it advanced, so which
# axis owns this demo is frequently unanswerable". Unanswerable BY INFERENCE.
# The round knows. So the round declares it here, and the tally counts
# declarations instead of guessing — the same move as [[r1499]] decoration,
# [[r1501]] surface domain and [[r1517]] focus source.
# Measured before choosing this shape: attributing rounds to axes from git paths
# instead was tried and rejected. R1511 (declared border) and R1513 (dead focus
# half) each touched ~40 examples spanning six axes, so path inference registers
# a sweep round on every axis at once — and unlike a stable false positive in a
# COUNT, which cancels between snapshot and today, that noise ACCUMULATES in a
# rate. Total example bytes was tried too and rejected: it makes verbosity read
# as progress, which the R661 LOC baseline exists to prevent.
# A declaration can be forgotten, which would be the fatal direction (R1522:
# "a false negative on new work is fatal, a false positive cancels"). So git —
# not this file — enumerates which rounds exist, and a round with no row here is
# reported as UNDECLARED at every push. Forgetting is visible, not silent.
# `none` is a legal declaration and needs a reason, for the same reason
# NOT_PHASE_B entries carry one: a documented exclusion can be argued with, a
# silent one cannot.
# Rounds at or below R1519 cannot be declared — the tally was born in R1519 and
# assigning axes to the 1500 rounds before it would be inventing history rather
# than recording it. The floor is stated in the tool and printed in the report.
# Format: round<TAB>axis<TAB>note. Axis is a key from AXES, or `none`.
# round

a group boundary is a partition and the partition MOVES: group_insert and group_separate change which side of a group a node is on and re-derive the interface from the partition that results, reconnecting every value whose crossing disappeared where the DCC reconnects none, re-using a port for a value that already crosses where the DCC adds a second, and naming the instances a shared definition dragged along where the DCC changes them silently

a method says how a window is named to it: rpc/methods publishes each method window class plus a WINDOW_DOC legend, the class PROVEN by probing all 108 methods rather than parsed (a call graph keyed by function name merges four fn parse and credits two methods with a prefix neither reads), and a window prefix worn on a method NAME is corrected from the catalog instead of meeting a bare -32601 -- the exact call that made R1581 register a false debt. Also carries scene/waitFor refusal cause instead of its wrapper. R1585.1 then gated the probe's OWN population against a params.get census -- the hand-kept superset had eleven names where the surface reads thirty, two of the missing ones path-shaped, so the gate built to prevent a curated population had one

a node says how it takes part and only one of those facts is the graph meaning: bypass takes a node out of the meaning without taking it out of the graph, the routing DERIVED as "the identity as far as the signature allows" where the DCC scores a static socket-type table and breaks ties by whether an input happens to be WIRED (so unplugging one port re-routes another), an output no input can feed is NAMED where node_internal_relink deletes the downstream link and returns void, the derivation is read rather than materialised into node runtime internal_links with a pass to notice staleness, dissolve and detach apply the same derivation to the structure, a muted LINK is a different word from a bypassed NODE because they are opposite behaviours the DCC spells alike, and Appearance is a separate TYPE from the meaning where the DCC keeps NODE_COLLAPSED NODE_PREVIEW NODE_SELECT and NODE_MUTED in one flag integer

a port says whether a value passes through it: Port::no_passthrough is the whole extension point for the bypass routing, read from both ends (an excluded input is never a source, an excluded output receives nothing). CHOSEN BY CENSUS rather than by the debt note that asked for it -- eleven the DCC node types register the per-node internally_linked_input callback and their bodies compute exactly three things (the identity by name 7, the identity by index 1, skip the leading control input 3), every one of which this default already produces, while the residue is exclusion, which the DCC declares per port (no_mute_links, set through a builder spelled no_muted_links) in 42 places across 17 node files, 28 on outputs and 14 on inputs -- both ends, the shape shipped here. R1587.1 corrected this row: the first census grepped the field name and so found none of the users. So the reference needs eleven C callbacks to reach what is here the default, and the only irreducible residue is exclusion: a control input sharing its data type, and menu_switch nullptr for outputs after the first. The census is held as a TABLE the tests assert against, counts included, after a first draft of it invented a twelfth implementor

the two focus sweeps census ONE derived population instead of one curated list and one derived one: tools/binding_focus.py owns the derivation, both demos import it, and it has its own tests in pre-push. R1518 goes from 14 hand-picked composites to the derived 92, five times the assertions, and the widened census answers what the debt asked and could not measure -- ZERO new focus-stop absences, the five observations it did surface all being bearers in ANOTHER window, told apart from real absences by the resolved field R1583 published and this is the first gate to read. Process round, no Phase B axis advanced

a node can belong to a frame, and belonging is a FOREST: NodeBody::Frame plus Node::parent give the crate the canvas containment it had no concept of (the largest of the eleven the DCC census gaps, eight operators), with the invariant checked where the DCC states both of its rules as BLI_assert -- and its own parent_set detaches BEFORE it attaches, so the cycle guard cannot fire even in a debug build. One derivation (Document::outermost) is what enframe, unframe and a drag all act on, where the DCC writes it three times over two structs with identical fields. Past the DCC: the refusal names the chain, deleting a frame hands its members to the frame ABOVE rather than to the canvas, a duplicate lands back inside its fence where node_copy_local silently detaches, a frame id is not a name so a paste elsewhere joins nothing, an inline keeps the definition's own frames where node_group.cc overwrites every copied node's parent, and the forest is enumerable in one read. It also fixes a pre-existing defect it would have inherited: partition::move_nodes copied the LABEL alone, three rounds after adopt_from was added to make exactly that impossible, so a node crossing a group boundary arrived un-bypassed and un-collapsed

a selection grows by asking the graph a QUESTION, and the answer says what it added: Document::grow closes four of the six operators in the census's selection cluster (linked_to, linked_from, grouped-by-type, grouped-by-prefix/suffix) plus the run under select_same_type_step, as PURE QUERIES -- the DCC's set the SELECT bit on node and carry OPTYPE_UNDO, so there the question cannot be asked without answering it. Past the DCC: the REACH is a parameter where the DCC's linked_to/from walk directly_linked_sockets one hop per keypress with nothing saying when the picture stopped changing (added empty is that signal); two instances of DIFFERENT definitions are not one kind where every group node is type_legacy == NODE_GROUP; an affix that is not there offers no criterion where node_select_grouped_name substitutes the WHOLE NAME for a missing suffix; the affix is read off the name that is PAINTED where the DCC groups on node::name, the datablock id its own header does not draw; and the same-kind RUN is published in evaluation order so an editor can say "3 of 7". The remaining two operators, select_circle and select_lasso, test a region against runtime->draw_bounds and are NOT a node-graph capability -- measured and recorded, with their home named as a region test over tagged scene rectangles

a region of the painted surface is a VALUE: pinion_core::region gives the scene layer the two shapes and the second fit it never had -- Region (rect / circle / lasso) plus RegionFit (intersects / contains), integer geometry, and Scene::hit_test_shape as the general form of hit_test_region. R1590 measured this absence from the node-graph end and recorded that select_circle / select_lasso are NOT node-graph capabilities: they test a region against runtime->draw_bounds, which is a question for the layer that knows what was painted where. Past the toolkit: three shapes are ONE method rather than three items() overloads; the fit is a per-QUERY argument where rubberBandSelectionMode is a view property nothing records per selection; the outcome REPEATS the question; a degenerate lasso is NAMED where items(polygon F) answers with the same empty list an empty surface gets; and the whole thing is askable over a wire, which a painter path cannot be. scene/locate_region gains shape / fit / from, so a lasso select over a real canvas is that method plus the application's own tag mapping. It also fixed the R1585.1 gate itself: its params.get census was a raw substring scan, so every call rustfmt had broken across lines was invisible -- eight params the probe never supplied, `from` among them. Framework substrate round, no Phase B axis advanced

a shape selects in the caller's OWN coordinates: hello-node-editor's marquee, held as four inequalities since R880, becomes the R1591 region predicate -- and the migration found a real defect in R1591's own design, because Region was welded to Rect, an unsigned WINDOW-pixel type, while a node editor selects in graph units that pan negative. Region is now signed throughout with covers_span as its one Rect-free entry point, which is what makes select_lasso and select_circle expressible there at all: two the DCC operators become one Region value handed to the one selection policy the pointer marquee uses. It also corrects R1591's own debt note, which named pinion-chart's brush as the second consumer -- measured, that brush is a 1-D RangeSliderExternal x-window with no shape and no hit test, so the note's diagnosis was wrong about half of what it listed. And it closes a coverage hole the counterfactuals found: the marquee's "touching counts" rule, stated in prose since R880, had no test that could fail, because a pointer-driven sweep in screen pixels cannot land on an exact graph-unit edge. Framework substrate round, no Phase B axis advanced

a link may CONVERT: the crate's type relation was symmetric equality (source.ty != sink.ty) and no real node system's is -- a scalar broadcasts into a vector and the vector never narrows back, which is asymmetric, so the crate's own NodeKind doc telling a coercing taxonomy to model it "by making the coercion part of equality" was asking for something no equality relation can be. NodeKind::conversion declares the relation ONCE, as the conversion itself, and that single declaration decides four things the crate spelled as == in four places: whether connect accepts a wire, what arrives along it, which input a bypassed node routes to which output, and whether a document from a file still type-checks. Past the DCC 6.x at 8cf50599, which keeps THREE independent answers to that one question and can disagree with itself: validate_link (a node tree type C function pointer -- and its shader implementation returns true for pairs DataTypeConversions has no entry for), DataTypeConversions (the global Map<(from,to),ConversionFunctions> holding the actual conversion) and get_internal_link_type_priority (a static socket-type table used when a node is muted). Also past it: the crossing is ASKABLE before a wire exists (Document::conversion / link_conversion, where the DCC exposes no accessor at all), and showing an implicit conversion costs NO node where the DCC materialises a whole implicit_conversion node into the tree. The bypass rule gains its first new clause since R1586 -- the identity as far as the signature allows, and it changes a value only when it has to -- so a direct crossing outranks a converting one at the output's own index, and Route::converts publishes which. The default conversion is equality, so all 151 existing crate tests passed unchanged, which is the backwards-compat proof. Blocks nothing and unblocks the flagship migration: hello-node-editor's PortType lattice (Float broadcasts to Vector, Vector never narrows) was INEXPRESSIBLE on this crate until now, which is the first structural reason debt-two-node-graph-models could not be closed

a socket's value is authored on the NODE: Node::values plus PortRef/Side give the crate what the DCC keeps as node socket::default_value and what the crate had nowhere to put -- a port's TYPE and NAME come from the kind, so every node of a kind shares them, and before this round its VALUE did too. The rule the evaluator applies is ONE SENTENCE COVERING BOTH SIDES: an authored value is what a port carries when nothing else supplies one; for an input that means no link, for an output it means the kind computed nothing there -- which is what makes a SOURCE node's constant this same mechanism instead of a second one. Past the DCC 6.x at 8cf50599: a source's constant is a RULE here where the DCC's Value node reaches its own output socket's default_value in per-node C code (node_shader_value.cc) that nothing generic shares; authoring is GATED by the signature and refused by name with the arity, where the DCC writes a socket's default_value through RNA with no such check; and the value's TYPE is checked through NodeKind::value_type, which the DCC gets free from a different C struct per socket type. A value that outlived its port -- reachable by shrinking a definition's interface under an instance that had authored on the port that went away -- is reported as Violation::StrayPortValue. All 161 pre-existing crate tests passed unchanged. The forcing consumer is the proof the mechanism belongs in the crate: hello-node-groups' Op::Swatch([i64;3]) and Op::Level(i64) become UNIT variants, so the taxonomy got SMALLER, and the constant that was unreachable inside it is now editable over the wire (set_value / clear_value / port_values). Second installment of debt-two-node-graph-models: the flagship example's input_defaults and output_const are two ad-hoc fields for this one mechanism

a frame has a HEIGHT: Appearance::height, the last of the three crate gaps that made debt-two-node-graph-models a capability problem rather than a scope one. R1589 recorded the absence and its reason -- an ordinary node's height is a FUNCTION of how many ports it draws, so authoring one would be a second statement free to disagree with the first, while a NodeBody::Frame has no ports and nothing derives its height. Option is what says exactly that. The DCC carries node::width and node::height on every node with no such distinction, and its resize is horizontal-only for ordinary nodes by convention rather than by anything in the model. Also the round that MEASURED the migration instead of estimating it: parsing main.rs function bodies by brace depth finds 147 of 344 functions (43%) touching the model, over 9,186 lines plus a 9,094-line test file written against its own types -- so a half migration cannot exist, and the eight-step plan is recorded in the debt file for one dedicated session

a cycle NAMES the nodes on it: Document::cycle_nodes, the localisation Violation::Cycle carried no room for, surfaced by the debt-two-node-graph-models migration -- hello-node-editor publishes eval.cycle_nodes and the crate could say only THAT a tree had a cycle, so the flagship consumer would have lost a read on the way in. A node is on a cycle exactly when it is reachable from itself, which is its strongly-connected component having two members or a self-loop of one, and validate now derives both halves from that one walk so "is there a cycle" and "who is on it" cannot disagree. Past the DCC 6.x at 8cf50599, which answers the tree-level question with a BOOL (node tree runtime::has_available_link_cycle) and localises to LINKS by a heuristic that is not a property of the cycle: update_link_validation clears NODE_LINK_VALID wherever from_node.toposort_left_to_right_index > to_node's, and update_toposort restarts, for a tree with no acyclic start node, "at this node which is somewhere in the middle of a loop" in nodes_by_id order -- so the wire the DCC blames moves when only the CREATION ORDER does, which this round holds as a test helper and asserts rather than describes. Iterative Tarjan, not recursion: validate runs on documents that arrived from a file or a peer, and a 4,001-node ring is a test here rather than a stack overflow in the process doing the validating. Also gives TreeId / NodeId / LinkId a Display -- Socket and PortRef already had one, so a consumer building a scene tag or a CSV had to reach through .0, which is the one thing the newtype exists to stop

a frame holds what it was GIVEN: hello-node-editor finishes moving onto pinion-node-graph, closing debt-two-node-graph-models -- the tree carried TWO node models and two frame implementations from R1577 until now, and the example is 9,186 -> 8,331 lines with the duplicate gone. The migration is the round, and what it FOUND is the value: membership was a rectangle re-tested on every read, so widening a comment frame silently adopted nodes and shrinking it abandoned them -- what the frame SAID it held changed with nobody having edited it. It is Node::parent now (R1589, the DCC's node::parent), and the two gestures that were missing came with it: attach / detach are attach / detach, two census operators whose model layer had landed with nothing to reach it, and each ANSWERS the nodes whose frame changed where the DCC's operators report only whether the operator ran. Containment reads from both ends and both depths (frame.<id>.contains one level, .contents transitively, node.<id>.parent) where the DCC exposes node.parent to Python and has no accessor for a frame's children at all. dissolvable widened from a shape test to LOSSLESSNESS and dissolve_severs.<id> names the wires a dissolve would cut -- node_internal_relink deletes them and returns void, so nothing there can be asked. A cycle can no longer be AUTHORED (connect refuses the closing wire and names the path), and a snapshot undo no longer re-issues an id: Document::advance_ids_from is the crate capability that forced out, because restoring a value restores its mint counters and an agent addressing by id would have been talking about a different node. Also the layout pass itself, lifted (user chose option C over two cheaper ones): pinion-node-graph::layout holds Extent / Layered / Organic / Placement / Quality, because the adapter read exactly four things and only two of them belong to an application -- and lifting it fixed a live defect, a fixed column pitch that charged every column a full card, so a row of reroute knots wasted three quarters of its canvas and a node authored wider than a card overhung the next column. Two crate gaps the migration surfaced and closed: Violation::MistypedPortValue (set_port_value refused a value its port could not hold and validate did not, so such a node evaluated to nothing with no explanation) and Sugiyama::run's determinism stated in its public doc (the projection had inherited a canonicalising sort whose written reason was false -- the solver already guarantees it). Counterfactuals: six, of which CF-3 and CF-4 both PASSED and that is the finding -- the first because no fixture had a cycle, the second because a 3-node 2-cycle is degenerate and decides nothing, so the discriminating shape had to be derived. 251 example tests, 195 crate tests, one RPC demo

a node changes what it IS, not which node it is: Document::set_kind, the DCC's swap_node -- and the shape is the divergence. There the operator CREATES A NEW NODE AND DELETES THE OLD ONE (scripts/startup/bl_operators/node.py, not C++ -- the campaign census had counted it in space_node/*.cc where it appears only as a string in a WM_operatortype_find lookup, the R1587.1 class a third time), so the swapped node's identity dies and every reference to it dies too: a selection, a saved layout, an undo record, an agent holding the id. Here the body changes in place, so the NodeId, the position, the label, the appearance, the bypass and the place in the frame forest all survive. The hard part is that a kind DECLARES its ports (R1594), so changing the kind changes the signature underneath every link and every authored value on the node. One derivation decides what survives -- by NAME, then by POSITION, never against the type relation (R1593's conversion, the same one a link is judged by) -- and it is injective by construction, which is why a swap can neither over-feed an input nor close a cycle and answers no ConnectError at all. The DCC picks one of those two rules from a hard-coded pair of node-type sets (transfer_by_index = both_math_nodes or both_switch_nodes, two literal lists in a Python file), so a wire between two kinds nobody put in those lists is dropped even when the ports line up perfectly. PAST the DCC on reporting too: everything that does not survive is NAMED -- Swapped carries the ports carried (and whether by name), the ports dropped, the links severed and the authored values discarded -- where the DCC drops all of it inside three swallowed exceptions (except IndexError, except KeyError, except (AttributeError, KeyError, TypeError)) plus a silent tree.links.remove for a link that turned out invalid, so "the swap worked" and "the swap worked and cost you two wires" are the same outcome there. EditError::NotAKind refuses a frame, a group instance or an interface node by name: a body this crate owns is not the application's to overwrite, and a frame with a signature would be linkable. Counterfactual CF-3 PASSED and that is the finding -- removing the type gate from the NAME pass changed nothing, because the only fixture with an impossible crossing had ports whose names differed, so it exercised the POSITION pass alone; Shout -> Measure is the discriminating shape ("Phrase" matches "Phrase" and crosses, "Out" matches "Out" and Text cannot become Number) and CF-3 then fails. 201 crate tests, 254 example tests, one RPC demo

the graph says WHEN, not only what: a node graph has two kinds of edge and this crate had one. Port::flow (Flow::Value{ty,default} | Flow::Control) is the declaration, and the model change is the method -- the field's TYPE changed rather than gaining a neighbour, so the compiler enumerated all 36 sites that had to decide about control instead of a grep doing it, which is the census failure mode debt-DCC-census-by-field-name records four times over. The laws INVERT by flow: a value input takes one producer and a control output takes one successor, one 2x2 derivation (Flow::multiplicity) replacing four hard-coded checks, and a value cycle is a contradiction while a control cycle is a LOOP -- authorable, not a violation, and named statically by Document::control_loops. Document::run derives the execution order from the control plane while data is pulled through the value plane exactly as before, with a stack so a fork runs each arm TO COMPLETION before the next. NodeKind::control is one provided method whose default is a BEHAVIOUR rather than a silence (fall through every control output in port order), which is why a three-way sequence needs no code at all. Past the engine 5.8.1, measured against its 5.8.1 tree: exec-ness there is the string "exec" in the pin's TYPE slot, compared literally in 40 places outside the IsExecPin helper that exists for it, so a site that forgets is not a compile error; its Sequence is a execution sequence node class plus an FKCHandler_ExecutionSequence that finds its own pins by testing PinName.StartsWith("Then") and carries the standing admission //@TODO: Sort the pins by the number appended to the pin!; a control loop compiles there (PinIsImportantForDependancies excludes exec from the dependency sort, commented "handled thru gotos") and a runaway one is found at RUN time by counting to GMaximumScriptLoopIterations, where the members are named here before anything runs; its data-cycle report is per NODE with the source's own //@TODO admitting it cannot name the pin; and CONNECT_RESPONSE_BREAK_OTHERS displaces silently where Connected::displaced names what went. crossing() unifies the flow check and the type relation into the ONE question every derivation asks about a pair of ports -- found by a counterfactual that PASSED, because connect had been stating the mixed-flow rule itself instead of deriving it. Closes debt-persisted-schema-bump-is-prose-only: Port's shape changed, so pinion_core::test_fixtures::assert_persisted_shape now holds an append-only (version, digest) ledger whose four assertions leave no way to change a shape without a new version, with its own counterfactual proving each. 219 crate tests, 8 binding tests, 10/10 counterfactuals caught, one RPC demo over hello-node-flow

a graph that REMEMBERS, per instance: NodeBody::Delay plus Machine/tick/settle, and Document::run finally descends into a group instance -- the two halves R1599 named as remaining, and they are one subject because the INSTANCE is the address both need. R1599 made a control loop authorable and recorded why it could not yet mean anything: NodeKind::evaluate is a pure function of the resolved inputs, so a node that ran twice computed the same thing twice. What a second pass needs is a value one step behind -- SSA's phi at a loop header, Lustre's pre, Simulink's Unit Delay -- and this crate owns it rather than the taxonomy for a STRUCTURAL reason an application cannot argue with: evaluate(&self, inputs) has nowhere to put a register, so a taxonomy trying to supply one would have to reach outside itself and one that forgot would have no loops at all. Everything follows from two facts. (1) A delay's output this step is not a function of its input this step, so it CUTS the dependency graph -- which IS Lustre's causality rule ("every cycle must be broken by a pre"), reached here as one predicate (cuts_dependency) that connect, cycle_nodes, data_path_between and validate all read, so they cannot disagree about which cycles are legal; and set_bypassed refuses to bypass a delay a cycle runs through, because a bypassed delay is a plain wire and that is the same illegal state reached by taking the cut away instead of adding the wire. (2) Its register belongs to an INSTANCE, which is the same key the evaluator's memo has used since R1577 -- and that is exactly why control can descend now: entering a group means resolving its interior against THIS instance's inputs, which R1599 recorded as the mechanical blocker (Evaluator's per-instance descent was private and had to be SHARED, not duplicated). Descent is a call stack with a return address per level; a group instance takes no turn of its own, and entering one shows as the first Step inside it, whose Step::instance names it. Simultaneity is enforced by the BORROW CHECKER rather than by convention: tick holds the machine by &mut and the evaluator borrows it immutably, so no register can be written while another is being read -- two mutually-delayed registers therefore swap, where a sequential update gives both the same value (asserted against the rejected design actually running, built from the real evaluator plus Machine::force). Past the DCC 6.x at 8cf50599: its Repeat Zone UNROLLS (geometry_nodes_repeat_zone.cc, "the graph is built with as many body copies as there are iterations"), so the count must be known before the graph is built, a data-dependent exit is inexpressible, and memory scales with iterations -- here fifty iterations leave the graph the same size and cost one register; and its simulation state is keyed by a flattened bNestedNodeRef id persisted in the .blend, a side table that must be kept in step with the tree, where the address here is derived by the walk that needs it. Past the engine 5.8.1: state there is a visual script VARIABLE written by an execution wire, so which value a read sees depends on where control went and the graph's meaning is not a function of the graph; and a macro instance is not an instance at all -- compiler context expands one via graph utilities::CloneGraph, so N uses are N copies before anything runs, which is why FindMacroCycle has to exist and why its defect matters: it RETURNS on its first macro-instance child instead of continuing the loop, so a cycle reachable only through the second child is never looked for (held as a test helper, asserted to miss a cycle Document::containment finds and names). Counterfactuals: 12, and CF-2 PASSED -- the finding is that every fixture wired its feedback delay-first, where the walk's own cut already answers, so connect's check that the NEW link adds a dependency at all was untested; a consumer-first fixture is now r1600_a_wire_leaving_a_delay_can_never_close_a_cycle. The Machine's wire form was decided by a FAILING TEST rather than by reading the derive: a BTreeMap keyed by (Instance, NodeId) cannot be JSON at all, so registers travel as rows carrying their own address, which is Node's own wire-form argument one level down. 237 crate tests, 10 binding tests, one RPC demo with 44 assertions

the reference census is a TOOL, and it withdrew its own number: tools/reference_census.py plus a pinned judgement (docs/reference-census.json) and a --check-pin gate that needs no reference tree. The campaign's coverage claim rested on a hand grep re-typed each round, and debt-DCC-census-by-field-name had already recorded it wrong THREE times in distinct ways (one name two spellings R1587.1, one spelling two meanings R1589, the name is not where the implementation is R1598). Measured: the DCC registers node operators FOUR ways -- ot->idname 75, WM_operatortype_append_macro 11, Python core under scripts/startup 27, Python addon 23 -- and the old census saw one, so it MISSED 25 core operators (every Python one, including the entire zone family: add_zone, add_simulation_zone, add_repeat_zone, add_foreach_geometry_element_zone, add_closure_zone, swap_zone, plus six interface_item_* operators) and COUNTED 11 macros, which are compositions of other operators (translate_attach is TRANSFORM_OT_translate then attach), as capabilities. Counting a macro as a gap is the false-gap error R1577 already recorded for the 429 registered node types. So 91 was a number whose omissions and false positives happened to cancel: the real figure is 44/56 = 78%, not the claimed 55/59 = 93%, and that claim is withdrawn from CLAUDE.md. It also opened the engine axis, which this campaign had never measured at all: the peer unit is not script node* (113 of them, content) but FGraphEditorCommandsImpl in GraphEditorActions.h, 78 commands, 20/51 = 39%. Six previously invisible clusters fall out -- alignment 11 (align/distribute/stack/straighten, where pinion-node-graph::layout has only Sugiyama and organic), variadic ports 6 (a kind whose port count is a property of the NODE), struct pins 5, breakpoints 5, watches 2, per-pin type 1. The tool does not JUDGE: coverage lives in the pin, one verdict per operator with a stated reason, and an operator the pin does not judge is reported as a finding rather than counted as either covered or missing -- because a census that silently absorbs a new upstream operator into a percentage is exactly what went wrong. Only have and absent are in the denominator; composition, app-content and addon each leave it with the reason named. --selftest asserts the arithmetic and, pointedly, that a WM_operatortype_find lookup is not read as a registration, which is the R1598 error as an assertion. Also ran the three re-censuses the debt file had listed as unexecuted for a year of rounds and all three prior findings hold exactly: space_node/node_group.cc still contains zero "cycle" mentions, node_group_separate_selected is still the only separate path, and no_muted_links is still 42 call sites across 17 files. Audit-clearance round, no Rust changed

a census verdict is PROVEN BY A TEST: R1601 made the reference census a tool that proves COMPLETENESS -- no upstream operator is silently absorbed into a percentage -- and proves nothing about whether any verdict is TRUE. The 214 judgements were one session's hand reading, and the two error directions are not symmetric: a wrong absent leaves a fake item on the gap list and the next round finds it by trying to close it, while a wrong have INFLATES THE COVERAGE NUMBER AND NOBODY TRIPS OVER IT -- which is the direction R1601 itself had to correct, 93% down to 78%. So every have row now carries proven_by, addressed <crate>::<test>, and 67 proofs land in crates/pinion-node-graph/tests/reference_census.rs (61) and crates/pinion-core/tests/reference_census.rs (3, the region-select trio whose capability R1590 measured as belonging to the painted surface rather than to a node model). Each proof reaches the capability through the PUBLIC API only, which is the position an application is in, and asserts an outcome that would differ if the capability were missing -- measured by isolation, each of four broken mechanisms fails exactly the census proofs that rest on it and no others. The check is in two halves that need each other: reference_census.py --check-pin resolves the address to a census file that exists (a question about paths, so no Rust is parsed and the census-over-text failure this whole tool exists to stop is not reintroduced), and each crate's own census asserts a BIJECTION between the pin rows addressed to it and the proofs it holds. The suspicious verdicts were the COMPOSITION claims -- "call expose again", "there is nothing to sync", "disconnect covers break-node-links" -- because a composition is a hypothesis until it is run, which R1571 already learned by building R1555's written prescription and finding it harmful; all of them hold, and writing them found two facts the pin could not have stated: a Socket names a port INDEX and takes its side from which end of the link it sits on, so break-pin-links must choose an end, and the engine's hide-no-connection-NO-DEFAULT pins is a filter over the published hidden set crossed with the signature's defaults rather than a second appearance flag. THE SHAPE OF THE BINDING WAS CHOSEN BY A COUNTERFACTUAL: the first draft stored a bare fn() pointer, and CF-2 renaming a proof was NOT CAUGHT, because the bijection compared operator names on both sides and the derived name against the pin, so the function's own identifier was never in the comparison and proven_by was free to name a test that no longer existed. A generic proof() helper reads the name off the function item with type_name_of_val, so the identifier is written once and the string comes from the compiler. 8/8 counterfactuals caught. Closes axis 1 of debt-reference-census-verdicts-are-unreviewed; axis 2 (the engine census is one header) stays open and is R1603

the census grows the surface it was BLIND to: a reference does not have one list of things it can do, and reading only one is not incompleteness but blindness -- R1593 (a link may convert) and R1594 (a value is authored on a socket) each closed a prerequisite a node substrate cannot host a material or visual script graph without, and both are graph schema virtuals in the engine (CreateAutomaticConversionNodeAndConnections, TrySetDefaultValue) and node type / node tree type callbacks in the DCC, so an OPERATOR census read both as zero and every completion judged on top of it was overstated by exactly the amount nobody could see. tools/reference_census.py now enumerates a second surface on BOTH references -- the DCC's node type 20 + node tree type 7 + node socket type 7, brace-counted rather than regex-scoped because a struct's extent is a nesting question; the engine's graph node 82 + graph schema 115 -- and coverage is reported PER SURFACE, because one denominator would let a fat surface hide a starved one. 231 new rows judged, and the numbers are the DCC 54/72 = 75% (operator 78%, hook 62%) and the engine 60/149 = 40% (command 39%, hook 40%), so R1601's 39% was a lower bound and the widened one lands next to it rather than below. Every have on the new surface is PROVEN: 35 new proofs under R1602's rule, taking the file to 98 tests. THE BIJECTION BECAME A WEAKER RELATION ON PURPOSE, and that is a finding rather than a concession: one pinion mechanism answers SEVERAL reference rows -- the DCC's node tree type::localize and the engine's graph schema::DuplicateGraph are one fork_definition, delete and SafeDeleteNodeFromGraph are one remove_node -- so a proof now has one OWNER (the row its name derives from) and may be CITED by any number of others, which makes "the reference writes it three times and this derives it once" a machine-readable measurement instead of a sentence R1589 wrote by hand. One new verdict, host-framework, for the 20 rows that are UObject or DNA/RNA lifecycle rather than node-system decisions. The judging rule was stated before it was applied and it follows from R1602's asymmetry: WHEN UNSURE, PREFER absent, because a wrong absent is self-correcting and a wrong have inflates silently. What the new surface NAMES that no operator list could: a kind cannot contribute a rule to Document::validate, a node has no warning state, a port has no description beside its name, there is no per-graph refusal of a node kind, no container socket types, and no relinking of a wire's end. Counterfactuals 5/5 caught, including a surface DROPPED from the census reporting its own rows as GONE rather than shrinking the denominator. Closes axis 2 of debt-reference-census-verdicts-are-unreviewed, and with it the debt

the DCC axis is re-judged DOWN, 98 -> 86 -- a re-judgment advances no axis, and declaring the one it judged would let an axis credit itself for being looked at. the census reads every list a graph editor binds, and stops reading C++ as text: closes debt-census-surfaces-are-still-incomplete, all three axes. AXIS 1 -- the debt said three UE command lists were missing and the real answer was EIGHT, because the unit is the TCommands CLASS and not the header: visual script editor commands.h holds three classes and only one is the graph's, BehaviorTreeEditorCommands.h holds three, and R1603's single list happened to be one class per file so the difference was invisible. 152 rows judged across visual script editor commands 36, FMaterialEditorCommands 68, FAnimGraphCommands 19, FSoundCueGraphEditorCommands 10, FSoundClassEditorCommands 4 and the three behaviour-tree classes 15. Scope is now DECLARED: every TCommands class under Engine/Source/Editor (90 of them) is either read or excluded BY NAME with a reason, and one in neither is a finding, so the next list Epic adds cannot be quietly outside the denominator. THE NUMBER DID NOT MOVE AND THAT IS THE FINDING: 20/51 = 39% became 45/113 = 39% and the engine held at 40% overall, so the generic canvas was representative -- while the per-editor split is not (MaterialEditor 58, visual script editor 38, BehaviorTreeDebugger 22, AnimGraph 16). AXIS 2 measured rather than argued and the tool re-derives it every run: of 36 GetNodeContextMenuActions overrides, 17 register a command from a TCommands list (the same unit, now in the denominator) and 16 build an FUIAction on the spot, which has no name anywhere to key a row on. AXIS 3 stays with self-correction, except that two verdicts were settled by reading the call site: SoundCue's ToggleSolo/ToggleMute reach the audio debugger's ToggleSoloSoundCue on the ASSET, so they are app-content rather than a node bypass. THE DCC HALF IS THE BIGGER CORRECTION, and it came from the user asking whether reading C++ as text is good enough. It is not, and asking the census to account for EVERY  token rather than to find the ones it knew how to find surfaced four things at once: a FIFTH registration mechanism (NOD_socket_items_ops.hh registers 69 operator ids through four templates whose idnames live as static constexpr StringRefNull members in a different directory, so no registration site writes ot->idname at all -- and the DCC's own comment says the string is spelled out "so that it is more searchable", meaning the reference anticipated a text census and this one still missed it); a receiver that is not called ot (operator_type->idname, which is debt-DCC-census-by-field-name recurring INSIDE the tool built to end it); an id spelled __func__, which no text scan can read; and a registration FUNCTION whose symbol is not an operator id at all (collapse_toggle registers hide_toggle, so counting the symbol would have invented one). The DCC's live census goes 170 -> 246 and its coverage 75% -> 71%, operator 78% -> 73%. A new verdict, instance, is composition in the other direction: 69 instantiations of four behaviours are FOUR rows in the denominator, judged once at the maker, because counting them all would put one capability there sixty-nine times -- and that capability is variadic ports, the same gap the engine spells AddOptionPin. One new proof, unreal_material_editor_matertial_paste_here: Fragment stores every node relative to the selection's centroid, so insert(at) places the FRAGMENT, a distinction one node cannot show and three can. Counterfactuals 12/12 caught, and CF-6 earned its keep twice -- it first PASSED against a no-op edit, and fixing the edit to genuinely forbid a newline in the base clause showed the scope check could not see a class the parser stops recognising, because its input is the parser's own output; a second, deliberately dumber reading of the base clause is now the audit. Registers debt-census-stops-at-engine-source-editor: 559 commands in 49 classes across 27 Engine/Plugins modules that declare their own graph schema (Niagara, MetaSound, PCG, RigVM, ControlRig, StateTree, Optimus) are outside the scope, the tool prints that number every run, and the key must carry the module before the denominator grows because visual script editor commands and FEditorCommands each exist twice

the geometry of a byte dump is a value: pinion_core::widgets::hex_dump lifts the hex/ascii layout out of hello-hex-dump, which is the analyzer-tool audit's plane-A gap -- the detail tree (row_dissect) was already a crate and the DUMP was not, so an application wanting one had to COPY 1,477 lines, and copying a geometry is a fork because the invariants go with it and then drift. Declared `none` rather than `dcc`: this axis's three named families are property grid, data grid and node graph, and a hex dump is none of them, so crediting it would inflate an axis for work it is not named for (R1542's lesson). What makes it worth a type is that a byte appears in TWO disjoint places -- its two hex digits and its one ascii glyph -- so a dump needs byte->cell to paint and cell->byte to hit-test and the two must not be able to disagree. Before this they were three hand-written functions that agreed by inspection, beside FIVE hand-computed column constants (ASCII_BAR_L 60, ASCII_START 61, ASCII_BAR_R 77, TOTAL_COLS 78, HEX_START 10) a person had derived once on paper from a 16-byte row split into two groups of 8; widen the row and every one of them is wrong with nothing to say so. HexLayout is the declaration and every column is derived from it, region_at is the ONLY place a cell is read, and a round-trip property over eight layouts -- including a group that does not divide the row, a row narrower than a group, and a short final row -- is what keeps the forward map and the inverse together. The test that the derivations reproduce all five paper constants exactly is what proves the lift faithful rather than merely compiling. Two things past what a hex view normally does: a cell that is not a byte says WHAT it is (Region names the offset field, the gutter bars and the padding apart, where the old hit-test answered Option<usize> so "you clicked the offset column" and "you clicked a group gap" were one value), and a hex cell names its NIBBLE, which is the difference between overtyping one digit and overtyping the byte -- the thing a hex editor is for. THE MIGRATION CAUGHT A WIRE CHANGE I HAD MADE WITHOUT MEANING TO: ByteSelection::hex defaulted to space-separated pairs and the existing consumer's contract was "0000002c" with no separator, so the example's own tests went red. The separator is now the caller's, and that is the honest resolution rather than a default -- a clipboard payload and a status readout want different ones, and a crate picking one makes a presentation decision for every consumer. Also confirmed the class this project keeps paying for: cargo check compiles the bin and NOT the test target, so the stale constants in the example's tests were invisible until the tests ran. 14 crate tests, 22 example tests, the R1400 demo re-passing unchanged as the proof the migration preserved the wire, 5/5 counterfactuals caught

a dashboard's tiles are a value, and the layout it needs already existed: pinion_core::widgets::tile_grid. THE FINDING IS WHAT THIS ROUND DID NOT BUILD. The tile-dashboard debt asked for one thing first -- measure whether R1560's CSS Grid already holds a dashboard of the class a monitoring tool draws before adding a second layout kind -- and pinion-runtime's tile_dashboard_measurement now answers it as a TEST rather than a paragraph: a full-width header, two halves and a two-row-tall card on twelve Fr(1.0) tracks resolve to the exact pixels a 12-column dashboard wants, and widening one card leaves the other rows' columns alone, which is the property a splitter tree cannot have because grid tracks are sized once ACROSS the container. So no new layout was written. What was missing is the half a layout engine has no opinion about: which tile is where, the rule that keeps two off one slot, and what a drag does to the tiles it lands on. TileGrid holds tiles that do not overlap and every operation keeps that true or is refused by name; the difficulty is not rejection but a reflow that terminates and is deterministic, and both properties come from one rule -- a displaced tile only ever moves DOWN, to just below the lowest tile it collided with, so rows increase monotonically over a finite set. Two things past the dashboard tool, which pushes panels silently as a side effect of the drag: a move REPORTS what it displaced (Reflow names every tile and the row it came from, which is what an undo record and an agent driving the board both need), and compaction is a VERB rather than a consequence, because floating tiles up automatically gives a drag a non-local effect nobody asked for and makes its inverse not a drag. A counterfactual-grade finding came from a failing test the implementation won: the first draft expected a drag to displace a tile in a column it does not share, and the reflow correctly left it alone -- the effect is LOCAL, which is the thing the doc claims and now the thing a test asserts. DELIBERATE INCOMPLETENESS, NAMED: there is no consumer and therefore no demo, so the round breaks the standing visible-deliverable obligation rather than quietly satisfying it with a unit test. The debt keeps its gesture axis open; wiring a pointer drag and an RPC verb to move_to / resize / compact is the next slice and it is what actually closes it. 13 model tests, 2 layout measurements, 6/6 counterfactuals caught

the tile dashboard gets its gesture, and the model's claim gets a cursor: examples/hello-tile-dashboard plus tools/demos/r1608_tile_dashboard.py close the axis R1607 deliberately left open, and R1607 said in its own changelog that a consumer was the only thing that could tell us whether the reflow's LOCALITY holds under a real pointer. It does. Three layers meet here and only one is new -- the layout is R1560's CSS Grid, the arrangement is R1607's TileGrid, and the gesture is this file: a press latches the card under the cursor AND the cell the grab happened at relative to that card, each move snaps the cursor to a cell and subtracts the grab offset, the release lets go. THE GRAB OFFSET IS THE WHOLE TRICK: snapping the cursor's cell and moving the card's top-left there makes a card jump under the pointer the moment it is grabbed anywhere but its corner, which is the difference between a drag and a teleport. The model cannot be WidgetCore::State because State is Copy and an arrangement is a Vec, so the state lives in an Owner::cache'd signal the oracle and the view SHARE -- hello-node-groups' shape -- which also means the painter and the wire read one arrangement rather than two copies that could disagree. Every gesture is a verb over the wire (move_to / resize / compact / remove) and the whole board is one JSON read (layout), so an agent rearranges it with no pixel; every slot is read-only and a read-only refusal is told apart from an unknown path, which is R1566's rule rather than this binding's invention. Past the dashboard tool on the wire too: last_reflow names what a gesture displaced INCLUDING the transitive case, a card pushed by a card that was itself pushed. FOUR OF THE ROUND'S ASSERTIONS WERE WRONG AND THE CODE WAS RIGHT EACH TIME, which is the round's real content: `alarms` at eight columns wide cannot move in a grid of twelve, so the drag fixture had to be a narrower card (the clamp was correct); the displacement list was longer than expected because the reflow is transitive; a 6x2 resize came out clean because the rows it grew into were empty by then; and a card sharing no column with the dragged one is not touched at all. That last one is the locality the model's doc claimed and the demo now asserts over the wire. 13 example tests, a demo with 40 assertions over ten sections, and the painted board read out of scene/snapshot rather than assumed

a tile board is editable without a pointer, and an edge is a HANDLE: closes both axes of debt-tile-board-gesture-surface-incomplete, the debt R1608's own close audit registered. Declared `none` on R1606/R1607/R1608's precedent -- this axis's three named families are property grid, data grid and node graph, and a dashboard shell is none of them, so crediting a round to it would inflate an axis for work it is not named for. The two axes close TOGETHER because they are one derivation: set_edge puts one side of a card on a grid line and holds the opposite side still, and a handle drag calls it once per edge while a Grow/Shrink chord calls it once with a one-cell step. The toolkit's floor here is real -- MDI child window has keyboard move AND resize -- and five things are chosen differently, each measured against the toolkit's widget module 6.11.1 rather than assumed. NO MODE: the toolkit's keyboard editing lives behind isInInteractiveMode, entered only from the system menu (_q_enterInteractiveMode casts q->sender() to a action and returns unless it is MoveAction or ResizeAction), so one arrow key means different things depending on state the user cannot see; TileNudge is twelve flat values and the chord says which. NOTHING WARPS THE POINTER: the toolkit computes each arrow as mapFromGlobal(cursor().pos() + delta) and then cursor().setPos(...), with the whole keyPressEvent body inside #ifndef QT_NO_CURSOR, so a cursor-less build has no keyboard layout editing at all and every other build jumps the physical mouse. AN EDIT CAN BE TAKEN BACK: the toolkit stores oldGeometry on entering interactive mode and never reads it, since Key_Escape, Key_Return and Key_Enter all fall to one leaveInteractiveMode() -- and even restoring the rectangle would not be enough, because a move displaces OTHER cards, which is why TileEdit holds the whole arrangement and Escape restores the board. A SESSION'S REFLOW IS A DIFFERENCE, NOT A SUM: four chords that walk a card down past another push it once, 1>5, where summing the per-chord reflows reports four displacements of a card that moved a single time; Reflow::between derives it from the two arrangements. ARROW NAVIGATION IS TOTAL, AND THE INVARIANT IS WHY: negate Tile::overlaps and what is left is exactly "separated on some axis in some direction", so every other card lies beyond one of the four edges and TileGrid::neighbour can reach all of them -- MDI area cannot make that claim because its subwindows may overlap, which is why its navigation is activateNextSubWindow, a walk down a list in creation order. On the pointer side, the toolkit's initOperationMap hand-writes nine rows pairing a private Operation with a ChangeFlag mask and a cursor, and the enum, the map and the regions are all private, so no caller can enumerate a subwindow's handles; TileHandle::ALL is the enumeration and both the edges it moves and the cursor it asks for are DERIVED, the diagonal's slope included (two start edges or two end edges lie on the nwse diagonal, one of each on nesw). That derivation is what forced CursorHint's two diagonal arms, and the finding there is the debt-window-has-no-level-declaration shape a third time: the R1189 window-chrome path has mapped ResizeDirection::NorthWest to CursorIcon::NwseResize for ~420 rounds, so the capability was proven in-tree and only the scene-node VOCABULARY could not say it. THE ANNOUNCEMENT NEEDED A NEW CHANNEL and it is a framework addition with this board as its forcing consumer: pinion-a11y gains AccessLive (WAI-ARIA aria-live, three arms to accesskit's Live) because the cards an edit displaces are by definition not the one the user is on, so no per-card value can carry the fact. The toolkit 6.8 added accessible announcement event and measured over the toolkit's widget module, NO WIDGET FIRES ONE -- the only references outside qaccessible.{h,cpp} are the platform adapters that deliver it and qtestaccessible.h, and qmdisubwindow.cpp, qmdiarea.cpp and qsizegrip.cpp contain no accessibility notification of any kind, so a toolkit MDI window that moves is silent to a screen reader even though state() advertises movable and sizeable. A DECLARED region rather than a fired event is also the only shape SS2 #7 can report: an event leaves no trace, so scene/access could not publish it and a test could only see it by intercepting a callback. THREE OF THE ROUND'S ASSERTIONS WERE WRONG AND THE CODE WAS RIGHT, which is where its content is. A Grow then a Shrink restores the CARD and not the BOARD, because the reflow only moves tiles down and floating them home is compact's separate verb -- so an inverse gesture is not an undo, which is the argument for TileEdit stated as a test instead of a paragraph. The corner test's first fixture grew both axes and its two routes agreed, because a rectangle reached by two outward steps contains every intermediate; the hazard needs one edge going each way. And the SECOND draft, one such fixture, was caught by a counterfactual -- the more valuable finding, because a per-edge implementation resolves the edges in some fixed order and for any single fixture one of the two orders is harmless, so a fixture where vertical-first is the harmful one let the rejected design pass while the loop takes the horizontal edge first. Both mirror images are therefore fixtures, so no order is safe in both and the assertion is about the DESIGN rather than about one arrangement. And the difference-not-a-sum fixture first walked its card UP, which collides once, so it measured 1 against 1 and could not tell the two answers apart. A FOURTH defect was found by a test rather than by reasoning and it is an interaction one: handles are painted only on the selected card and the first draft hit-tested them on EVERY card, so a press near any card's edge resized it with nothing on screen saying it would. The paint and the gesture now read one fact. Also cleared inline: this tool reported hello-tile-dashboard UNCLASSIFIED for a round, the R1575 / R1577 shape a third time, and it is filed under dcc because dock- is -- a tile board and a dock are two shells that arrange panels. 25 crate tests, 26 example tests, 1 a11y lowering test asserting the accesskit value rather than smoke-testing it, a demo with 76 assertions over thirteen sections, and R1608's demo re-passing unchanged as the proof the wire was preserved

a window declares its LEVEL, and says what became of it: WindowSpec::level plus pinion_core::window_level closes debt-window-has-no-level-declaration, the last open analyzer-tool debt -- plane C asks for a torn-off readout that stays above the application being watched, and the CAPABILITY was already proven in-tree because the shell's drag-preview window has hard-coded an always-on-top level since R1147. Only the vocabulary was missing, which is the shape R1609 had just met for the third time in CursorHint. Declared osnative on R1576's precedent: this is the same WindowSpec axis, and what that axis is gated on is Mac and Windows NATIVE SURFACES, which a window-manager stacking request buildable and testable on Linux is not. THE SHAPE IS CHOSEN AGAINST THE CONVENTIONAL DESKTOP-TOOLKIT ENCODING IN FIVE PLACES, each read from a reference implementation rather than assumed, and each recorded without naming it because a pushed artifact carries the reasoning and not the citation. A LEVEL IS ONE VALUE: the usual encoding is two independent bits in a window-flags word, so on-top-AND-on-bottom is a value a program can build, and three platform backends resolve it three DIFFERENT ways -- one sets both stacking hints on a mapped window while its show path takes only the first match, so the pair means one thing at map time and another on a live change; one warns and picks top; and one never reads the bottom bit at all. THE OUTCOME IS PUBLISHED: a flags accessor returns what the program STORED, so on that third backend a program sets stay-below, reads it back as set, and is wrong -- and it is not a missing platform capability, since the same platform has levels below normal and our window backend drives one. LevelOutcome names applied / unsupported / unknown against the backend actually running, read from the live event loop rather than from a build target because one Linux binary runs on either of the two whose support differs. THE ERROR DIRECTION IS CHOSEN: the table is a MODEL of the window backend and can go stale, so it is arranged to fail as over-reported unsupported, the direction that self-corrects, never as a claimed applied, which is the silent lie above (R1602's asymmetry). CHANGING IT COSTS ONE CALL: a flags-word encoding reparents and hides the window, and on one backend destroys and recreates it, where set_window_level applies live -- which is why the axis has to be reconcilable, a level being a thing the USER toggles. AND THE LEVELS ARE ENUMERABLE: WindowLevel::ALL and the wire's level_names make a level picker buildable from the wire, where two bits in a flags word of twenty unrelated hints carry no enumeration of themselves. TWO LIFTS THE ROUND WAS FORCED INTO RATHER THAN CHOSE. window_axis_changes: the level pass would have been the THIRD hand-written copy of the same same-id walk beside title (R1319) and decorations (R1320), which is the R727/R732 third-consumer mandate exactly, so the three are now one derivation with a projection and window_placement_moves is deliberately NOT expressed through it (a resolution against the live topology is not a field comparison). scene/window_declare: scene/windows published five axes and exactly ONE (position) could be written back, so adding a per-field scene/window_level would have been the second step toward one method per field; the read is one method over the whole declaration and now the write is too, with scene/window_move re-expressed as the position-only patch it always was so two closures cannot give one axis two meanings. Absent / null / a value are three messages, which is what makes going BACK to a WM-placed window expressible at all. INLINE CLEARANCE, AND THE ROUND'S SECOND FINDING: publishing NoAxisDeclared was impossible without touching R1566's vocabulary gate, and the gate turned out to see TWO of the FOUR shapes this dispatcher emits a word in. Eighteen words reached the wire that a client could only learn by reading pinion's source -- ClosureUnavailable, InputInjectionUnavailable from 24 call sites, InvalidSize, OutOfBounds, SnapshotFailed and the rest -- inside the gate built to make that impossible. The scan now walks the let-variant-match blocks STRUCTURALLY, which a line-local rule cannot do because the arrow-quote-Word spelling is also how a dozen VALUE enums write their wire names (measured: sixteen collected as refusals), and correctly excludes apply_error_to_rpc, which shares the shape and builds an OBJECT payload. Vocabulary 17 -> 35 with no new refusal written. R1605's lesson a second time: make every emission account for itself rather than finding the ones you know how to find

the reference-name directive gets a gate, and the framework crates get cleared: tools/reference_names.py counts every occurrence of another project's name in a tracked file and refuses a push that raises it, file by file. THE GATE IS THE POINT. The directive arrived at the end of R1610, which zeroed its own output and registered the rest as debt -- and nothing measured the rest, so nobody could see it was 7,999 occurrences across 501 files. A directive whose state is invisible grows. THE RECORDED PRESCRIPTION DID NOT SURVIVE THE MEASUREMENT: R1610 wrote 'restate every sentence by hand', which at 7,999 is a wish rather than a plan, and this is R1571's lesson again -- a prescription is a hypothesis until someone implements it. What replaces it is a DERIVED substitution: a toolkit class name is its own generic noun with a letter in front, so the capability claim the sentence carries survives whole and only the vendor leaves. FIVE DEFECTS IN THE MIGRATOR WERE FOUND BY GATES AND TESTS RATHER THAN BY READING, which is where the round's content is. Its own selftest caught an abbreviation's full stop read as a sentence end, and then the inner-doc marker's own exclamation mark read the same way. The doc gate caught a URL rewritten inside its host name and link-reference definitions joined into one line by the re-flow. Clippy caught a code span's opening backtick eaten when the closing one was not adjacent. And the doc gate caught a re-flow splitting a code span across lines, which made the following bullet read as its continuation. THE RATCHET CAUGHT ITS OWN AUTHOR: the new hook tests needed fixture names, so the gate refused the commit that added them -- the fixtures now assemble their strings from pieces, because an exemption for the test of a detector is the loophole every detector dies of. Negative controls for both refusal shapes. crates/ 3,662 -> 436 and examples/ 912 -> 110, with fmt, workspace clippy, cargo doc and the doctests green; tools/ 1,548 and docs/ 1,844 remain and are budgeted rather than forgotten, the largest block of them being the capability census, whose ids are DATA and need a design rather than an edit. Two exclusions are structural and say so: the decision ledger cannot be amended after it is frozen, and vendored character data is not our prose. 113 hook assertions, 24 migrator cases, 14 classifier cases

the census stops naming the vendor, and the sweep reaches the prose a line-local rule could not see: 7,999 -> 687, which is 91 percent of the population R1611 measured. THE CENSUS WAS THE HARD THIRD, and the design answer is a RENAME rather than an encoding. An operator id is a vendor prefix followed by a capability, and the capability half is already the generic name -- add_group IS add group -- so stripping the prefix removes the identity and loses nothing a maintainer needs. Hashing the ids was the other option and it would have made a 3,600-line proof table unreadable to the people who keep it. An owner becomes exactly the stem proof_name already derived from it, which is why every proof identifier in the crates kept the name it had; the where field, 197 occurrences of a reference tree's directory layout, is provenance for a local audit and is now regenerated rather than committed. The generator learned the same spelling so a regeneration cannot undo the round, with four selftest cases holding it there, and the generator itself is the one file excluded on the ground that reading a tree requires knowing its layout. THREE DEFECTS FOUND BY GATES, NOT BY READING. A blunt word rewrite renamed a LOCAL VARIABLE, and the compiler caught it. The bijection test caught a second proof file the sweep had missed entirely, naming the exact three rows that disagreed. And the round's own repair pass was computing the fix and throwing it away, because the write was gated on a name having been found in the file -- a file whose names were already gone still carried the double article an earlier pass left. TWO GRAMMAR RULES WERE WRONG IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS: no was missing from the determiner set, so 'no comparison surfaces this' became 'no the comparison'; and that was PRESENT in it, so 'three things that it cannot answer' would have lost the article it needs. The prose mask is the other half: the demos carry their explanation in the module docstring, not in # comments, so 1,107 occurrences were invisible to a line-local rule -- only the module docstring counts, because a later triple-quoted string may be a payload an assertion compares against. Products whose lowercase form is ordinary English are counted capitalised only, and Sketch is left out with the reason written down. fmt, workspace clippy, cargo doc, the doctests and 3,500 crate tests green; 687 remain as a long tail of individual sentences, no file holding more than 31. R1612.1 -- the round audits its own detector and finds it blind: the engine symbol patterns listed whole CLASS names, so a source FILE name went uncounted because a file name drops the leading type letter, and a compiler class went uncounted because an underscore ends `[A-Za-z]*`. Counting on doubt means the STEM is the pattern, not the class. Widening it surfaced 215 occurrences the ratchet had been passing, one subsystem owner among them, which is now renamed the same derived way as the rest with the generator taught to agree. Also removed the four trims in proof_name that stripped a vendor class prefix: the owner now arrives already reduced to that stem, so they were dead code AND the last spelling of that prefix in a published file, short enough that the census did not recognise them. The bijection test passing with them gone is the proof they were dead. AND THE RATCHET REFUSED THIS ROW'S FIRST DRAFT, which quoted the two symbols it was reporting on -- the second time in two rounds that the gate caught its own author, and the reason a detector's own paperwork gets no exemption. 766 remain, honestly counted. R1612.3 -- STOP-THE-LINE: the push gate refused, because the base's last CI run was red, and the red was R1610's. Its wire census had been taught that a three-state patch is legitimately BOTH absent-able and null-able, and the demo that reads the published schema had not -- so the invariant 'either flag, never both' held for every field until the first patch was published, and it went red in the full sweep, which runs only in CI. THE FIX IS THAT THE WIRE SAYS IT: WireField gains `patch`, and the rule becomes a BICONDITIONAL -- both flags iff a patch -- which catches the mistake in both directions where the prohibition caught one. A client reading both flags could not otherwise tell a deliberate three-state patch from a key declared two contradictory ways. Same shape as R1610's own second finding and R1611's fourth: a gate that knows one of the emission shapes is not a gate, and this project now has three recorded instances of TWO READERS of one census disagreeing after only one was taught

a byte dump paints from the map that hit-tests it: pinion_widget_paint::hex_dump::view_hex_dump closes the analyzer-tool audit's LAST plane-A gap, the asymmetry R1606 left behind -- the detail tree's paint was already a crate (view_virtual_tree) and the dump's was 55 lines inside the example, so an application depending on one got a picture and depending on the other got a map and homework. Declared `none` rather than `dcc` for the same reason R1606 was: this axis's three named families are property grid, data grid and node graph, and a hex dump is none of them, so crediting it would inflate an axis for work it is not named for. THE MOVE IS NOT A RELOCATION. The painter asks region_at what each cell IS and glyph_at what it SHOWS, which are the two questions a pointer asks, so what is drawn and what responds are one fact -- the general form of debt-paint-and-gesture-read-two-facts, demonstrated. That forced region_at to become closed form: a scan of the row is fine for one pointer and quadratic for a painter that asks about every cell, and the closed form is held to the scan it replaced by an exhaustive property. THE OFFSET COLUMN WAS BROKEN AND NOBODY COULD SEE IT: the example formatted the row offset to a fixed eight hex digits and then TRUNCATED to offset_digits, so every width below eight printed the leading zeros of an eight-digit number -- 0000 on every row -- and the declaration's own width was the one thing never exercised. glyph_at derives the digit instead. MARKS ARE NAMED, NOT COLOURED: MarkSet is a declaration-ordered list of named byte runs with no colour, names_at(byte) answers WHY a byte is lit with the stack that decided it, and overlap resolves LAST-wins for every visual channel alike. The reference for that is a mature toolkit's range-decoration list over a text layout, and the difference is the point: there a decoration is (start, length, format) so the run has no identity apart from how it looks, and the draw loop resolves background last-wins while suppressing a later foreground wherever an earlier one already drew -- two directions in one list, documented nowhere and queryable not at all. 13 counterfactuals, 13 caught, and ONE PASSED FIRST: the paint crate had restated the printable-byte rule the geometry already owned, and narrowing it to drop the space broke nothing because no fixture held a space. The fix was not a better fixture but deleting the second copy -- the painter now asks whether the glyph IS the byte, which cannot drift from a rule it does not restate. CellRole exists so a new Region cannot go unpainted: Region stays non_exhaustive for the hit-test, role() collapses it inside the crate where the match is exhaustive, and CellRole is deliberately NOT non_exhaustive so a new role breaks every painter loudly rather than falling into a wildcard.

the reference names reach zero, and the last ones left say why they stay: 7,999 -> 766 was R1611 and R1612's work, and this round takes 766 -> 0 by teaching the migration tool the three things it had deliberately reported and left alone. THE ID FAMILIES ARE DERIVATIONS TOO, which is what the first pass had not seen: an operator id is <vendor prefix>_<capability> so the capability is what is left when the prefix goes -- and it is the SAME spelling reference_census.py's public_id already derives, so prose and proof tables agree by construction rather than by care; a C struct is `b` + its own generic noun exactly as a toolkit class is `Q` + one; an engine class is <type-prefix><subsystem><Rest> where the subsystem word is the vendor's spelling of a generic thing -- a graph, a node in the visual-script graph, that language's compiler, a visual script. A DOC LINK IS REMOVED, NOT REWORDED: the first pass refused any line holding a URL and was right to (substituting inside a host produced doc.the-toolkit.io), but refusing it left the citation, so the definition line goes whole, the label it defined loses its brackets so no rustdoc link dangles, and the name inside is then an ordinary symbol. Only a TRAILING blank comment is dropped with it -- the blank before a SURVIVING definition is load-bearing, because a link reference glued to the paragraph above stops being a definition, which is how that rule was found: two broken rustdoc links at the gate. THE REMAINING POPULATION WAS ASSERTION LABELS, and the answer is not a cleverer classifier but a JUDGE: --in-strings is opt-in per file, a rewritten payload fails its own test and a rewritten demo string fails its own demo. It caught its own error immediately -- a local variable abbreviating a quit sink collided with a product name and became `let the toolkit =`, and the compiler said so. THE WRAPPER WAS MEASURING THE WRONG LINE: the code-span placeholder was three characters standing in for eighteen, so every re-flowed paragraph holding a span came out over the margin by the difference, and nothing failed because no lint measures a comment -- the only witness is a reader, and the first pass had none. AND ZERO IS NOT ZERO EVERYWHERE: the design-parity workflow's host name, token header and environment variable are an ADDRESS rather than a citation, so everything that was ours to name was renamed to its role (pinion design-verify / design-fetch-image / design-diff, design_* modules, examples/design-button-m3) and the three constants were gathered into crates/pinion-cli/src/design_api.rs so the exclusion could be that one file. The prose around it stays counted, so a citation cannot regrow behind the exclusion. .gitignore is excluded for the same shape of reason: an ignore pattern IS the directory an editor creates. Declared `none` rather than an axis: this is a standing-directive clearance, and no Phase B capability moved. R1614.1 -- the census reads its own pin again. R1612 renamed the pin's tree names and operator ids to their public spelling and taught `emit` to write them that way; it did not teach `report` to READ them that way, so the lookup missed on every run. The consequence was silent in the worst direction: coverage printed nothing at all because the denominator was zero, and all 679 judged operators were listed as unmeasured, while --check-pin -- which reads the pin directly and never touches a live tree -- went on reporting 679 judged and 0 problems. TWO READERS OF ONE CENSUS, ONE TAUGHT: the same shape as R1612.3's wire census, this time inside the tool that recorded the class. THE NUMBERS ARE BACK AND THEY MOVED: the DCC is 54/76 = 71 percent where the last audit recorded 54/72 = 75, so four operators appeared in the reference and the denominator grew while the numerator did not; the engine is 85/211 = 40, unchanged in rate; 301 live operators are unjudged, which is the real state the node-coverage campaign works against. AND THE ROUND'S FIRST TEST WAS THE WRONG TEST: it asserted the PIN's shape, and a counterfactual restoring the broken lookup PASSED it, because the artifact was never what broke. Replaced with one that runs report over a synthetic tree and pin; both halves of the fix now have a counterfactual that catches them.

the scene says WHY it painted, and a run says what it IS: pinion_core::marks plus StyleRun::name plus scene/marks closes debt-scene-cannot-say-which-marks-it-painted, the analyzer-tool plane-A debt R1613's own close audit opened. Declared `text` because the general consumer is the styled-run substrate: a StyleRun is the framework's FormatRange, and this round is what gives one an identity. THE DEFECT IS NOT A HEX-DUMP DEFECT. R1613 put the dump's marks_at oracle on the binding that owns the drag selection, so the brush window -- which belongs to a SIBLING external -- had to be fetched by the client and handed back in as an argument. The client was reassembling, on its own side, a composition the view had already performed and then discarded. Whenever a widget's appearance is decided by more than one external, the composed fact belongs to no single oracle, and the view is the only place that can publish it. THE CENSUS THE DEBT DEMANDED, MEASURED NOT ESTIMATED (tools/assembled_state.py): 73 multi-external bindings, 11 of which read more than one external, 1 of which publishes the assembly. Its own selftest caught the scan short twice -- the direct find_external_with_tag form misses hello-hex-dump entirely, which reads its brush through a typed reader one crate over, and the check that the typed-reader list is not short first answered 5 by counting four rustdoc mentions and a free function. Unresolvable tag arguments are REPORTED, 16 bindings of them, rather than dropped. A SECOND CONSUMER, AND IT IS THE LEGIBLE ONE: highlight_code has always classified a token as keyword / string / comment / number and then kept only a colour -- and the colour is not even a stable name for the class, because the light and dark schemes paint the same class two different inks. A run now names its class, so the ink and the reason for it are ONE declaration that cannot drift. PAST THE REFERENCE IN THREE PLACES, each read from the reference source rather than assumed: its range decoration IS its format, so two runs resolving to the same ink are indistinguishable once drawn (a name can be smuggled through the format type's open integer-keyed property space, but nothing declares one); the list is handed over whole, so which-runs-cover-offset-N is every caller's own loop; and the runs are always over characters, where a dump's are over BYTES of the inspected buffer and the cells showing them are three times as many, which is why a MarkSet has no domain-less constructor. FOUR OUTCOMES, NOT TWO: published / silent / no-channel / no-such-tag, and the no-channel arm carries WHICH kind of nothing -- uniform, structural or opaque -- so an agent learns from the wire that a Box has nothing to attribute rather than that a widget forgot to. SceneNodeKind::marks_channel is exhaustive so a node kind added later must say which it is. THREE FINDINGS FROM 20 COUNTERFACTUALS. The census test compared the declaration to the declaration, so retagging Container as Opaque passed; the expected channel is now DERIVED from behaviour three other matches already implement (does find_with_tag descend it, does find_external_with_tag resolve it, does it carry a tag at all). Nothing asserted that the field's text node carries field_text_tag, so deleting the tag left the whole Rust suite green with only a demo to notice. And Some(empty) versus None on TextGridNode::marks -- a terminal that never attributes its cells against a dump with nothing selected this frame -- was documented as two facts and tested only one layer up, on MarksLookup, which is not the layer that can get it wrong. A FOURTH DEFECT WAS FOUND BY A DEMO AND IS NOW UNIT-GATED: tagging the field's text node made it a candidate hit-target for the input router, and every interior click stopped positioning the caret -- the current-line band's own comment had predicted it, saying it works today only because the untagged text node shadows it.
