a call must be declared first: the transport now asks the declaration BEFORE it dispatches, on both channels, so a name absent from `$schema` is absent from the wire. Declared `api` -- it is the RPC surface's own contract, the axis whose open items are exactly "what a client may bind to". THE DEBT THIS CLOSES HAD HALF ITS DIAGNOSIS WRONG, and finding that out was the round's first act: R1632 recorded that an External's declared action list "does not reach the wire at all", measured against `rpc/methods` and `scene/snapshot`. Both measurements are true and the conclusion is false -- the list has been on the wire since R825 as the reserved `$schema` introspect PATH, not a `scene/*` method, so a census run on one axis reported absence about something living on another. What was actually missing was the ORDER of two questions: the transport dispatched first and consulted the declaration only to explain a refusal, which left the dangerous direction -- implemented, never declared -- working perfectly and unobservable. R1631's `arrange` was callable and undiscoverable for a full round with `cargo test`, clippy, the demo and the push gate all green, because none of them had two lists to compare. THIS IS THE REFERENCE'S FLOOR, PROVED BY COMPILING IT: a toolkit 6.4.2 class with one `slots:` method and one plain one, driven through the toolkit's meta-object -- invokeMethod ran the declared name and answered true, refused the undeclared one with false and indexOfMethod() == -1, and its 6.11.1 source still emits the same "No such method" from the meta-object's own translation unit. The toolkit reaches the guarantee by codegen; pinion reaches it by gate, because its surfaces are hand-written -- and gets one report out of that the meta-object cannot express, `DeclaredButUnhandled` (the surface published a name and did not answer it), split out of `UnknownInvokePath` so an agent doing the right thing and an agent guessing are no longer told the same word. TURNING THE ORDER AROUND MADE THE TREE SAY WHERE IT WAS WRONG, which is the answer the debt file said was impossible from source text: 123 undeclared or mis-declared actions (56 never declared, 67 declared as READ slots and dispatched as verbs -- `$schema` saying "query me" about names only `invoke` answers), plus 2 on the read channel, one of them `pinion_widget_paint::dock`'s `lifecycle` whose own doc calls it "surfaced as scene-as-data via query(lifecycle) (§2 #7)". `pinion-audio`'s two Externals had their ENTIRE invoke surface undeclared while the type doc described all ten verbs in prose. Five names carried BOTH channels at one address (bump/boost/restamp/dense/focus_region) and a field holds one channel, so whichever was declared hid the other -- split into a tally and a verb, which is what the reference does too (a property and its setX() are different meta-object namespaces). Three surfaces hand-copied an upstream declaration and were moved to `SchemaField::concat`; `hello-tab-reorder`'s copy had already lost `send` and demoted `move` and `grab_cancel` to reads. THE SOURCE CENSUS FAILED THREE TIMES and what caught each miss is recorded: it read only the first match, then missed tuple-pattern arms (`("bump", Int(n)) =>`, found by a DEMO dying), then missed `if path == "..."`. The final method was to over-report every string literal in an invoke body and classify by hand -- and the general lesson is that the wire gate RETIRES the census, because an undeclared action now dies in its own demo. Eight counterfactuals, 8/8 caught after the first run of CF-7 PASSED and was a finding: nothing anywhere asserted a declared read reaches the wire, because every `lifecycle` assertion in the tree calls the trait directly. The test written to fix that found three more mis-declarations in dock on its first run, and its first oracle ("every declared read answers") had to be replaced -- it reported fourteen text_field paths that answer None because the widget is UNBOUND, which is a fixture that cannot discriminate; asking the surface's own dispatch instead needs no binding and is exact.

an action says what it takes: ArgForm (Undeclared / Path / Nullary / Scalar / Object / Delimited) plus SchemaField::action_with plus SchemaArg::optional plus ArgDomain::OneOf, so a declared verb carries its argument grammar and not only its name. Declared `api` -- it is the same RPC contract axis R1637 advanced, and this is the half R1637 left unsaid. THE ROUND STARTS FROM BEING BEHIND THE REFERENCE, which is rare enough to say plainly: a meta-method publishes each parameter's name and type and generates that list from the signature, while pinion published `{"path": "arrange", "channel": "invoke"}` and nothing else -- 45 of 45 actions on one surface, measured over the wire at R1637. An agent could discover a verb existed and still had to read our source to call it. SILENCE IS AN ARM, AND THAT IS THE ROUND'S CENTRAL DECISION. 487 actions are declared in this tree and the overwhelming majority take an argument nothing describes, so making an empty `args` mean "takes nothing" would have converted every one of them into an affirmative false statement -- the error direction R1602 records as the expensive one, because a wrong `have` inflates silently while a wrong `absent` self-corrects. `Undeclared` publishes NO `args` key at all and `Nullary` publishes an empty list, so a client can tell "has not said" from "takes nothing". The reference cannot represent the first state at all, because a generated parameter list is always a claim. PAST THE REFERENCE IN TWO PLACES: an argument says where its values COME FROM rather than only its type -- `OneOf` for a closed vocabulary and `ValuesOf` for a live path on the same surface -- where a meta-method gives a type name and constrains only enum-typed parameters through its meta-enum; and `optional` marks the segments a delimited payload may elide, with the invariant that they must be a SUFFIX, which is forced by the only form that can elide anything. EVERY CLOSED VOCABULARY IS PROJECTED FROM ITS DEFINITION, NOT WRITTEN OUT: `Axis::WIRE_NAMES`, `Edge::WIRE_NAMES`, `ArrangePass::WIRE_NAMES` and `VoicePolicy::WIRE_NAMES` are const-evaluated from each type's own `ALL` through its own `name()` / `as_wire()`, and `ALL`'s length is the `VariantCensus` arm count -- so a new variant is a BUILD failure rather than a vocabulary quietly one short on the wire. That projection is what makes a literal domain defensible at all; a hand-written list would be exactly the disconnected census R1630 exists to end, and the `ArgDomain` doc now states the line between a model-derived bound (never a literal) and a code-derived vocabulary (a literal, projected). ARRANGEPASS IS THE CRATE LIFT THIS FORCED: R1631 turned the reference's eleven commands into an axis, an edge and a gap and left the fourth parameter -- WHICH pass -- as four string literals matched at the call site, which is the same shape one level up. It is now a value with `ALL` / `name` / `from_wire` / `tail`, and the example dispatches through it. THE WIRE RENDER IS DERIVED RATHER THAN CHOSEN, which closed a latent defect in the same edit: `$schema` was two hand-written shapes and the one carrying `args` had silently dropped `channel`. Nothing had noticed because no constructor could produce a field that was both parametric and an action, so the arm had no inhabitants -- `action_with` gives it inhabitants, and an action that said what it takes would have rendered as a path a client may read. A BLANKET SUBSTITUTION WAS TRIED AND REVERTED, and the reason is the round's sharpest lesson: attaching the composite send grammar to all 67 `send` declarations produced FALSE CLAIMS, because `send` is at least four different grammars under one name (20 composite, 11 bare event name, 6 accepting both, 15 hand-rolled). The discriminator that let it through was "does the file mention `split_send_payload`" and the mention in `pinion-audio` was a DOC COMMENT -- the third time this session a text census read something that was not code. The grammar is now declared once in `composite_tag::SEND_ARGS` and pointed at by the 24 declarations whose decoder was verified by CALL SITE; the other 43 stay silent, and the four-grammar collision is registered rather than papered over. THE SUFFIX INVARIANT CAUGHT ITS AUTHOR ON ITS FIRST RUN: `key` was declared optional because the bare-target wire is `":<Event>:<token>"`, and that segment is present-and-EMPTY rather than elided, so it made `event` follow an optional argument. Eight counterfactuals, 8/8 caught -- one had to be re-authored because removing a line left an unused binding and so did not compile, which the driver reports as testing nothing. A demo that builds `arrange`'s payload OUT OF THE SCHEMA -- separator, segment order and vocabularies all read off the wire -- and lands all eight published combinations, refuses two unpublished values by name, and then follows an argument's declared `values_path` on the audio surface to a live voice id.

a widget publishes the events it accepts: `#[derive(WidgetEventName)]` emits DRIVABLE_NAMES as a const projected from the EXTERNALLY_DRIVABLE_EVENTS the statechart codegen already emits, and the eleven bare-event `send` declarations point their argument's domain at it. Declared `api` -- the same RPC contract axis as R1637 and R1638, closing the first of the three choices the send-collision debt named. THE COMMONEST ACTION IN THE TREE WAS THE LEAST DESCRIBED. R1638 gave an action an argument grammar and could describe none of these: the legal names are per widget and existed only as a runtime `Vec`, reachable when a refusal was being worded and nowhere a schema could point at. So the vocabulary was discoverable ONLY BY GETTING IT WRONG -- R1564 made the refusal name the accepted set, which is a good refusal and a poor contract, because it asks an agent to make a call it expects to fail before it can make one it expects to succeed. A TRAIT METHOD CANNOT BE CONST, which is the whole reason this needed the derive rather than a helper: an argument's domain is a `&'static [&'static str]` evaluated at compile time, and `as_name` is a trait method. So the macro emits the arms TWICE -- once as the trait's `as_name` and once as an inherent `const fn wire_name` -- which is duplication a generator does and an author never sees, and the const is then folded out of the codegen's own drivable list. The set a client reads, the set a refusal advertises and the set `from_name` admits are one list BY CONSTRUCTION. INTERNAL EVENTS STAY UNFORGEABLE, and that is what makes publishing safe: the projection is over the DRIVABLE const, not the variant list, so a chart-raised `ButtonActivate` is absent from the published set and refused on the wire. A schema reader who assumed every event of the machine was callable would have been wrong, and the demo asserts both halves. THE SIX DUAL-GRAMMAR SURFACES WERE DECIDED RATHER THAN LEFT: datepicker, disclosure_group, listbox, radio_group, table and text_field decode a composite payload AND fall back to a bare event, and `ArgForm` has no union arm. It deliberately gains none -- a declaration states what a client SHOULD send, and a shorthand the surface also accepts is a convenience rather than a contract, so the composite form is declared because it is the one that stays true if the shorthand is retired. Same call `pinion_audio::play` made for its bare-string form; the union question is left where it belongs, in the debt that owns the collision. A CONSTRUCTOR COULD NOT BE WRITTEN AND THAT IS RECORDED: `SchemaField::send_event(returns, names)` was drafted and removed, because a `const fn` cannot build the `&'static [SchemaArg]` a field needs out of its own parameter -- a function argument is not promotable. The helper is therefore at the ARGUMENT level (`SchemaArg::event`) and the call site writes the one-element slice in a `const` block, which is where promotion is legal. The reason is in the doc so the next round does not re-derive it. A catalog walk now refuses to let a `send` be silent (and refuses an empty vocabulary, which is the shape a widget whose chart drives nothing externally would publish); it found the two dual-grammar surfaces in the catalog on its first run. Four counterfactuals, 4/4 caught. A demo that drives TWO different widgets -- one example would pass against a shared global list -- plays every published name through the real wire, checks that a refusal still teaches the set, and asserts the composite surfaces declare four segments and which of them may be elided.

the catalog walk is every widget surface, and its escape hatch is not free: the channel checks R1637-R1639 built now construct all THIRTY-NINE `ExternalIntrospect` impls in pinion-core's widget directory rather than the nineteen whose constructors took no arguments, and a completeness gate holds the list to the source. Declared `api` -- these are the gates that keep the RPC contract true, and a gate covering half its population while reporting a pass is the shape this round removes. THE DENOMINATOR WAS STATED NOWHERE, which is what made the gap invisible: the walk built what was easy to build, passed, and read as coverage. Measured when the debt was registered: 19 of 39, with `TableExternal`, `ListBoxExternal`, `RadioGroupExternal` and `ToolbarExternal` -- four large composite-send surfaces -- among the twenty nobody had ever checked. Widening it found a real mis-declared channel in the first run (`ColumnResizeExternal`'s `send` was declared a READ slot and has always been dispatched through `split_send_payload`), which is the same hit rate the walk had on its first run against dock. THE ORACLE HAD A HOLE AND A NEGATIVE CONTROL CLOSED IT. The channel check asked "does the surface's `invoke` answer this declared read with anything other than UnknownPath", and a surface that declines EVERY name with one stated sentence answers that yes for names it has never heard of: `ButtonStateSnapshot` and `ToggleStateSnapshot` refuse uniformly ("this surface is a read-only copy; drive the live button external instead"), and three of their declared reads were reported as mis-declared channels on the first widened run. The walk now probes an invented name first and compares the shapes -- a surface that answers a name it does not know the same way it answers a declared one is telling us nothing about either. Three false positives out, one true positive left. A FUZZY COMPARISON INSIDE A COMPLETENESS GATE IS ITS OWN FAILURE MODE: the first draft matched a snake_case catalog label against the type name by lowercasing and dropping underscores, and four entries that WERE in the catalog came back unaccounted (`row_dissect` against `RowDissectionExternal`). The labels are now the type names and the comparison is an exact set difference. AND THE ESCAPE HATCH IS NOT FREE -- a counterfactual adding a reason-less exclusion PASSED against the first draft, making the gate's own opt-out the cheapest way through it. An exclusion must now state a reason of real length AND name a type that is actually in the source, so a stale exclusion cannot silently shrink the denominator either. The source scan follows R1605 rather than counting: it collects names and every name must be in the catalog or in the stated exclusions, so a mis-parse surfaces as an unaccounted NAME a reader can act on rather than as a number that happens to match -- which matters because this session burned three times on text censuses that read a comment, a tuple pattern, and only the first match. Four counterfactuals, 4/4 caught after two were re-authored: one did not compile (removing a catalog entry orphaned its import, and the driver reports that as testing nothing) and one was the finding above. 32 demos over the surfaces whose declarations moved, all pass.

a number and its unit sit on one line: AlignItems::Baseline plus LetterSpacing { Normal, PxX100, EmX1000 } plus the first written statement of which whitespace a measured box contains. Declared `text` -- letter spacing is a character format property and the R1560 audit records the character half as unchanged since R1546; the baseline work is the layout primitive that half of a type scale is useless without. THE ROUND IS A CONSUMER REPORT, and the first thing it cost was a design that was already wrong. A field report from a repo that git-rev-pins pinion ported a production design system to an all-Korean product UI and reported three things; two of them were mis-scoped by ME before the reference was read, and the user asking whether the reference had been compared is what caught it. THE FIRST MIS-SCOPE: the report said letter_spacing: i32 cannot hold four of its five tracking values (-1.5 / -0.5 / -0.3 / +1.5 px; only -1 fit) and pointed at `as f32` downstream as proof nothing blocked a float. True, and the repair is not a float -- TextStyle derives Eq + Hash and that participates in the 5.16 paint-fragment cache key, so a float takes both away. Fixed point keeps them. But precision was only the reported symptom: the reference toolkit's font takes a spacing MODE beside the value -- a percentage of each glyph's own natural advance, or an absolute length -- so spacing being specifiable RELATIVE TO THE FONT is the existence floor, and a scale restated per size is what a scale exists to avoid. So the field is now a type shaped like LineHeight one type above it -- the same either-or, absolute device units or a fraction of the font -- rather than the finer i32 I had already written and tested. Em-relative rather than the reference's advance-relative, stated as a deliberate difference: parley takes ONE absolute per-cluster spacing, so an advance-proportional form cannot be resolved to a single number, and that is registered rather than glossed. Thousandths not hundredths because tracking lives at 0.01-0.1 em where two digits quantise a scale coarser than its own values. THE SECOND MIS-SCOPE, AND THE ROUND'S SHARPEST FINDING: baseline alignment looks like a missing enum arm and mapping AlignItems::Baseline to TaffyAlign::Baseline would have shipped a variant that MOVES NOTHING. taffy 0.7.7 types its measure callback FnOnce(..) -> Size<f32> with no channel for a baseline, so every measured leaf returns first_baselines: Point::NONE and flexbox does baseline.unwrap_or(height) -- which for a text leaf IS the box's bottom edge. Measured, not read: the naive mapping places the pair at exactly End's relative offset (both 53px), and the test says the baselines are still 10px apart. That is the wrong-`have` direction R1602 names as the expensive one, and it was one line away. What ships instead computes each participant's baseline BEFORE layout and injects the difference as taffy margin.top, so the row's own height is the layout engine's answer about the shifted children rather than a correction applied after it -- a test asserts the row still contains what it moved. TextBox gains baseline: Option<f32> for the same reason it gained line_count at R1344, a fact only the measure knows; Option rather than a synthesized fallback so a measure that reports nothing takes its item OUT of the alignment visibly instead of aligning every row slightly wrong. The 5.37 self-hosted engine reports the SAME LineBoxMetrics::baseline_px its paint arm draws on. Non-text items keep Start where CSS synthesizes from the bottom margin edge, and that boundary is documented as a boundary: a synthesized baseline needs a laid-out height, which is exactly what computing before layout does not have. THE THIRD OBSERVATION WAS ONE SYMPTOM WITH TWO CAUSES and the report had merged them. Trailing whitespace reproduces on the first run -- the intrinsic measure is parley's width(), documented as "excluding the width of trailing whitespace" -- and LEADING whitespace does not; it is measured. A fix aimed at full_width() would have closed one half of what was filed as one thing. The choice is correct (CSS removes a flex item's trailing whitespace) and was written down nowhere, so it is now a test plus the paragraph on TextNode that sends a reader to `runs` BEFORE they reach for two adjacent nodes -- the report's own framing was that runs' documentation is excellent to someone who already found runs. Two nits closed the same way: PathPoint / Stroke name their constructors, because non_exhaustive rejects a struct literal and rustc's E0639 does not say what to call instead; and WidgetCore's trait doc now says #[widget] exists, since 57 examples use it and the consumer hand-wrote the impl and filed the required event_name/title pair as missing defaults -- it HAS them, the type leading you there did not say so. Two counterfactuals, 2/2 caught, one of them re-authored because deleting the call left dead functions and so did not compile, which tests nothing. Four debts registered, two of them existence-floor gaps this round surfaced and did not close (no word_spacing at all, though CSS, the reference and parley all have it; and advance-relative tracking, blocked upstream).

a conditional argument declares its cases: ArgDomain::OneOfWith plus ArgCase, so an argument whose value decides the REST of the call says so, and the two verbs that need it (arrange, item) are declared from the model own answers. Declared api -- the same RPC contract axis R1637-R1640 advanced, and the round also re-judges api 65 to 72 and text 90 to 92, both STALE at the push gate. THE DECLARATION WAS NOT SILENT, IT WAS WRONG. R1638 described arrange third segment as one slot, string domain open optional, which is the only sentence a flat positional argument list can produce about a segment that is a closed edge vocabulary after align, an integer after stack, and ABSENT after distribute and straighten. Measured over the wire before the fix: that declaration admits nine calls and the dispatcher refuses three of them (align:horizontal elided, align:horizontal:17, stack:horizontal:start) and ACCEPTS AND SILENTLY IGNORES a fourth (distribute:horizontal:start). Silence would have been honest; that carried a schema authority, which is the wrong-have direction R1602 names as the expensive one. And item could not have been fixed by a flat list at any price: add:in:1, remove:in:0 and move:in:2:0 are three different ARITIES, so no positional list describes them, and item published no args at all. THE CASE TABLE HANGS OFF THE DISCRIMINANT for R1593 reason, restated: which values may I pass and what does that value then require are ONE fact, and a declaration that splits them lets them drift, exactly as link legality and link conversion became one declaration so may I draw this and what arrives if I do could not disagree. PAST THE REFERENCE, AND THE REFERENCE PROVES ITS OWN CEILING: a meta-method parameter list is generated from one C++ signature, so a conditional argument there has to become SEPARATE METHODS -- which is what the toolkit does, and R1631 folded exactly those eleven alignment command names into parameters. Its one concession is the Cloned attribute, the synthetic shorter overloads a default argument generates, which enumerates arities and cannot say two of them belong to different values of one parameter. So a client there discovers seven unrelated verb names; here it discovers two verbs and seven cases, which is the same information plus the fact that they are two operations. THE TABLE IS PROJECTED AND THE PROJECTION IS GATED AT COMPILE TIME. ArrangePass::tail and the new ItemEdit::tail answer what a verb reads after its shared segments, each tail answers required, and the case arrays are const loops over ALL -- so a new pass or edit cannot arrive without a case. What cannot be projected is the SchemaArg itself, because pinion-node-graph is pure data and must not depend on the framework to name one, so the argument name, type and vocabulary are spelled at the declaration and a const assertion (ArgCase::adds) holds the pair to the model facts: swapping which tail may be elided is now error[E0080] by name, not a schema that lies. THE RULE IS ONE DEFINITION WITH THREE CALLERS: SchemaField::conditional_defect refuses two discriminants, an optional discriminant, a shadowed argument name, an expansion that puts an optional before a required, and a nested case table -- the last forbidden not because the append rule breaks down but because an unexercised wire shape is a claim no client has been held to. Seven unit tests drive it, one per arm plus a legal control, because a checker that refused everything would pass every refusal test. THE GATE STATES ITS DENOMINATOR: no pinion-core widget declares a case table, so the workspace walk asserts the INHABITANT COUNT IS ZERO rather than reporting no defects over an empty population -- R1640 finding applied to the gate written the round after it. A SIDE-EFFECT FINDING, SAME CLASS ONE SEGMENT ALONG: item side was declared as the closed pair in and out, but which side ANSWERS is the selected node kind business, so the pair advertised calls the surface refuses. It now points at a live path (item_sides) that empties when no call is well formed. 13 counterfactuals: 5 caught by unit tests, 2 caught by the const build gate and therefore scored BROKEN by the harness (debt-counterfactual-cannot-score-a-build-gate, second and third instances -- confirmed by hand that the E0080 message is the assertion own), and 6 by the demo after CF-10 PASSED and was a real fixture gap, since nothing had ever selected two nodes and read the live domain. A 40-plus-assertion demo builds every call the declaration admits from the wire alone -- separator, segment order, per-case arguments, and both the present and elided forms of anything optional -- lands all 20 of them, and refuses eleven calls the declaration excludes including the one that used to be accepted and ignored. R1638, R1631, R1632, R1637 and R1639 demos re-pass, R1638 own payload builder rewritten to read the case table since that is what it claims to do.

the declaration gate reaches every surface: paint_catalog plus every_catalog plus a two-area completeness scan close debt-the-declaration-walk-reaches-one-crate, and the nine demos R1637 left red in CI are green. Declared api -- the same RPC contract axis R1637-R1642 advanced, and this is the round that pays its unpaid bill. STOP-THE-LINE, AND THE RED WAS SIX ROUNDS OLD. CI had failed on every push since R1640 and the sweep named nine demos; all nine reproduce locally and deterministically, so none is a flake. Every one is R1637 declaration gate firing on a surface no local gate can see, in three distinct kinds. ClickRouter::click had been declared with SchemaField::new -- a READ -- since R683.C, while invoke is the only thing that answers it and query returns None, so the declaration was wrong in BOTH directions at once; three demos refused with PathIsAReadSlot. hello-node-flow declared twenty-one reads and ZERO actions while act dispatches ten verbs, the pinion-audio shape R1637 found, in an example R1637 source census could not reach because the binding landed at R1599/R1600 and the census was a hand classification of invoke-body string literals; two demos refused with UnknownInvokePath. And four demos over hello-answer-origin walk every declared slot through query, which R1637 made false for an action. THE FOURTH KIND IS THE SHARPEST: that walker exists FIVE times, and R1641.6 repaired the fifth copy -- a Rust unit test -- while its own blast-radius note read the two sibling UNIT walks and not these four. The shared definition was not missing either: assert_declared_channels_are_true has been in rpc_verify since R1566, seventy-seven rounds, used by exactly one demo. So the duplication was not for want of an abstraction, it was for want of a POINTER to one, and what R1643 adds is the small piece those four walks each need -- declared_read_paths, the filter -- rather than a whole-surface assertion they would have to be rewritten around. WIDENING PARTIALLY IS INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM A PASS. The first wiring routed two of the three channel checks at every_catalog and the third still iterated catalog -- and the third was precisely the one whose oracle catches ClickRouter. Counterfactual CF-1 found it: the case that was supposed to prove the widening PASSED, which is the finding, and the fix made it CAUGHT. THE WIDENED WALK THEN FOUND A REAL MIS-DECLARATION ON ITS FIRST RUN: SplitterExternal.send is also declared READ and also dispatched by invoke -- the same hit rate the walk had on dock (3 on its first run) and on the 39-widget widening (1). Repaying it published PointerWireEvent::ALL and WIRE_NAMES, projected from the enum through a const spelling of as_wire_name, because the surface accepts exactly the five names from_wire_name admits and had no way to say so. A FOURTH COPY OF THE ARM LIST WENT WITH IT: the round-trip test in input.rs carried its own hand-written five-element array, so a sixth event would have left the one place that checks the round trip silently short. AND THE RATCHET ITSELF HAS A HOLE, found by counterfactual and registered: variant_census(all) holds ALL LENGTH to the arm count and cannot see an arm written TWICE. Replacing Cancel with a second Leave keeps the length right, publishes PointerLeave twice, loses PointerCancel entirely, and left the whole workspace suite green -- including the round-trip test written in this very round, because walking ALL and asking from_wire_name(WIRE_NAMES[i]) == ALL[i] is satisfied by the duplicate. R1630 had already recorded the argument that closes it (total plus surjective plus equal cardinality implies injective) and the test had only the third term; a distinct-set check supplies the second. Registered as a general debt because every ALL in this tree has the same hole and this round closed one. THE COMPLETENESS GATE IS PER AREA, NOT POOLED: each source name is compared against ITS OWN area catalog, so a fat catalog cannot account for a starved one. 8 counterfactuals across three gate scopings, and the scoping itself taught something: CF-5 PASSED against a gate that excluded pinion-core, the crate holding the guard it was testing -- the harness own rule 2 (a scoped gate cannot say NOTHING catches a break) applies to package selection and not only to test filters. Final: 6/6 caught, the two example-side cases confirmed against a demo-inclusive gate because the walk deliberately does not reach examples and the demo is what gates them.

a run can be stopped, stepped and watched: pinion-node-graph::debug -- Breakpoints, Watches, Session, Timeline, Paused, and Command::STRIDES as the 2x3 product of Direction and Stride. Declared `dcc` -- the node-graph third of that axis, and it closes the DEBUGGING cluster the R1604 judgment names among the engine's eight (breakpoints 5, watches 2, stepping): the census's engine half moves 51% -> 62% and its tree-debugger command list 2/9 -> 9/9. THE DESIGN IS ONE SENTENCE: A BREAKPOINT CANNOT CHANGE THE RUN. The debugger suspends nothing. It computes the whole run once, WITHOUT REFERENCE TO ANY BREAKPOINT, and then moves about inside it -- so the property is structural rather than promised, and it is bought by R1600's decision that state is a delay and nothing else, which makes a run a pure function of the document and the registers. Nothing weaker would do: a debugger that halts a running machine observes a DIFFERENT execution from the one the program has without it, and reverse stepping then has to replay recorded frames -- which is exactly why the reference's tree debugger has CurrentValues and SavedValues as two commands over two data sources. Here they are one object, asserted: the readings are identical at two positions while the trace prefix is not. FIVE STEPPING COMMANDS ARE TWO WORDS. Widened to 600px, with the cramped case asserted as a STATED no-op rather than an unexamined one. THE THIRD WAS A MODEL MORE PRECISE THAN ITS SCREEN. FieldType declares six shapes and the painter drew two, so a boolean was a box somebody typed `true` into and an integer knew its bounds with no way to step inside them. RowBox::options generalises to RowBox::parts -- every affordance inside a control, published as a tag suffix and a rectangle -- and the painter and the consumer's hit test both ITERATE that list, so a shape added later cannot arrive with two copies of its geometry. A boolean gets a checkbox, an integer gets a stepper pair that CLAMPS by the bounds the field declares (the control refuses to leave the range instead of the gate reporting it afterwards), a list gets one row per element plus the row that adds one, split by the same FieldType::elements the encoder uses so the screen and the document cannot disagree about what a comma means. THE FOURTH WAS A GATE THAT DID NOT NAME ITS POPULATION. The demo's backward direction accepted any tag under seven family prefixes wholesale, so `all 136 painted tags are declared` was true of far fewer than 136 elements. Each family now carries a MEMBER COUNT: it cannot say which element arrived but it fails the moment one does, which is R1650's pin-the-member-set shape. The report says what it means now -- 100 declared element by element, 42 pinned by count across 8 families. lab.link's pin is DERIVED from the specification rather than a constant, because a family whose size is a function of the graph must not be pinned to a number or authoring a link fails the wrong check. Verified with a real mouse over a mapped window: the checkbox, the stepper (65535 -> 65534) and the list's add row all answer a physical click.

the screen is compared to its specification FROM THE PIXELS IT PAINTS, and the first run of that comparison found the screen was not painting them. Declared `none` -- like R1650 this round builds an instrument and pays defects with it, and the repairs land on hello-node-lab, whose own rounds already declared `catalog`. THE GAP: `tests.rs` asked the geometry HELPER where each control is, and the helper was right every time; the only thing that had ever compared the reference screen to the painted scene was a python demo needing a live process, which no local gate runs. Three consecutive rounds shipped a paint/hit-test disagreement through that hole (R1648 double offset, R1651.1 rail seats in the wrong frame, R1652.1 a list drawn over the field below it) and an AUDIT found all three. THE INSTRUMENT IS A FRAMEWORK CAPABILITY, not a test helper. NodeVisit now carries the walk's geometry -- the accumulated offset, the enclosing clip, and absolute_rect() folding both -- so EVERY painted node can be asked where it is, including the ones nobody tagged. That is the load-bearing part: a text run carries no tag, so every tag-keyed gate in this tree is blind to it, which is exactly how R1649 stacked a whole shell's card text down the left edge with 118 wire assertions passing. Measured against the mature toolkit the same day: its scene item reports an absolute rect that IGNORES an ancestor clip (a 500x500 child of a 30x30 clipping parent reports 500x500, and a fully clipped child is indistinguishable from a visible one), its widget maps to an absolute position that ignores the scroll area hiding it, visibility is a SECOND call, a text run inside a control is not an object and has no geometry API at all, and there is no single-pass index -- so this is superior on four counts and the None return is why: reported and visible are one fact here instead of two. THREE DESCENTS BECAME ONE. try_for_each_node adds the exit the searches needed, so rect_for_tag_absolute and absolute_rects_by_tag and for_each_text_leaf are now one recursion with three accumulators -- the scroll's path transparency, its offset fold and the clip intersection had been written out three times and were free to disagree. THEY ALREADY DID: the index skipped a first match that was clipped away and let a later duplicate fill the slot, where the lookup returned None and stopped, while the doc claimed they agreed arm for arm. Unified on the rule that makes the early exit SOUND -- the first node carrying a tag decides, including when it decides nowhere. WHAT THE FIRST RUN FOUND, in a screen four rounds had called a reproduction: every label in it FLOWED. A TextNode carries a rect that reads like a position and is not one, and without a LayoutStyle the engine stacks it under its predecessor -- so the toolbar's readouts, every card's rows, the gate panel and the hint strip were painted in one column, 28 of them outside the node that owns them and some past the bottom of the window. The sibling shell learned this at R1649 and this example was written afterwards without it. Then: a pan to the LEFT underflowed the pane-local conversion, which is a panic in a debug build and a coordinate near four billion in a release one, on a gesture the hint strip advertises -- and the canvas had no clip at all, so panning the other way painted the graph over the palette. Repaired with the substrate rather than a clamp (ScrollAxis::Both over a world surface, the shape hello-node-editor already uses), which is also what makes a card scrolled out of view report absent instead of misplaced. Then: pins held a fixed size while cards scaled, so at the minimum zoom a dial pin and its neighbour's accept pin covered the same pixels and the second could not be pressed. Then: two labels overflowed the palette, and three pairs of labels had overlapping boxes -- a box IS the promise now, because a run wider than it wraps over its neighbour as soon as the string grows, and the strings here are user data. AND THE WIRE HAD THE SAME SPLIT. scene/bbox is documented as the method an agent computes screen coordinates with, and it answered the node's OWN rect -- fine until a pane scrolls, then it addresses nothing. Measured: the demo read a card at (2207,2081) in a 1440x900 window and the click was refused as out of bounds. It now answers BOTH, named for what each is: `bbox` unchanged, plus `window` with the offsets folded and the clips applied, null when nothing of it is visible. A `tag` locator joins `path` because a tag is the same word click routing already resolves by, so measure-then-press is one vocabulary. A gate caught the consequence immediately -- rpc/methods publishes this method as one that parses a window prefix, and refusing two locators first made that false. THE SWEEP VISITS EIGHT STATES, not the one the specification describes, because R1652.1's defect only exists in a state nobody had ever looked at. The pan state is driven through the app's own drag handler rather than by writing the pan, since a state a test invents can be one the screen cannot reach. 5 counterfactuals, 5 caught after one was a FINDING: deleting the grown-list state left every assertion green, which made that state decoration -- so the floors moved onto the sweep itself (state count, busiest state, total probed), because a state that is deleted takes its own assertions with it. Verified: 20 example tests, 3374 core, 1201 rpc, the 15-section wire demo, and the real render read back as a PNG. What this does NOT see is stated in the module rather than implied: every rectangle is the box a run was GIVEN, not the extent of its glyphs, and a string too wide for its box still wraps over what is below it -- there is no elide anywhere in the tree (the two places that say "elided" are prose describing behaviour no API provides), so that is a framework gap with its own note and not an oversight here.

five defects the running window reported and every test had missed, and the one that was a question became a capability. Declared `catalog`: TextOverflow's eliding arms are widget-catalogue vocabulary every run in the tree now has, and the settings-form painter is their first crate-side consumer. THE ARM WAS DECLARED AND NOBODY IMPLEMENTED IT. TextOverflow::Ellipsis has been on the wire, in the footprint census and parseable off a text field since R47.5, and both painters carried a note saying they fell back to a hard cut -- the GPU adapter's "silent fallback to Clip until R47.x" and the terminal walker's "R51.111+ adds the ellipsis policy". So a caller asking for an ellipsis got a cut and nothing said so, which is worse than the absence: an absent capability sends a consumer looking for another way, a false one is believed. R1653's own debt note said the capability did not exist at all -- its census searched for `elide` and the type is spelled `TextOverflow`, the one-spelling census error this project has a standing note about: a census that searches for one word reports the existence of the same capability under another as zero. THE POLICY IS SHARED AND THE METRIC IS NOT. "How wide is this string" has two legitimate answers here -- shaped pixels and terminal cells -- and they cannot be reconciled, so `pinion_core::text_elide` takes the metric as a closure and the cuttable offsets as a list: parley cluster edges on one side, grapheme boundaries on the other, one decision about which end gives way. Five arms now (the reference has four modes plus a wrap switch), and they are a property of the RUN rather than a metrics helper the caller must remember -- measured on 6.11, its label class has no elide property at all, only its item views do, and a label handed a string too wide for it clips while its size hint still reports the full natural width. AND THE ELIDED STRING IS PUBLISHED, which is where this passes the floor rather than matching it: measured, `text()` there returns the authored string and the elided form exists only inside the paint call, so no automation or accessibility client can say what a reader saw. `scene/text_painted` reports every run with its window rect, what the scene holds, what the frame drew, the ink extent, the line count and whether the ink left the box. That last field is the user's own question -- "why can the wire not diagnose text leaving its rectangle" -- and the answer was that every read published the box the author PROMISED and none published what the shaper produced. THE SCREEN NOW FILLS ITS WINDOW, and both halves had to move: the pane rectangles were constants, and the window was `SizeStrategy::Fixed`, which pins the resize FLOOR at the open size. A layout that follows the window is no use if the window cannot be shrunk. `use_viewport_size` already existed and this screen simply did not read it. The reason no test saw it is the sharpest thing in the round: every check ran the layout pass at WIN_W x WIN_H, so the assumption and the defect were the same number, and the sweep now publishes the size the way the shell does and asks the screen to lay out at three of them. THE GROUP BEHAVIOUR IS THE REFERENCE'S. Its nine frame verbs include deriving the frame's rect, hit-testing it, applying a node to it and dragging it; this screen had frames as rectangles out of the specification table, so a host did not grow when a card was dragged in, did not shrink when one left, and could not be moved. The rect is now derived from the members' bounding box, the tab is the handle (the interior belongs to the cards, or a group would swallow presses over its own members), and a drop re-parents through the crate's own `set_parent`. TWO CLAMPS FOR ONE FACT, AND THE TIGHTER ONE WON: a node stopped dead partway up the canvas because `clamp_to_world` bounded the position to the world surface and a `.max(0)` on the next line pinned it at the origin -- the world's negative half exists so a node can be dragged up and left, and nothing could reach it. The rail's seven destinations were a bullet and a smaller bullet in a 12px face; they are marks drawn out of scene primitives now, one per destination, since vendoring a glyph font is forbidden in this tree. THE GATE EVERY DEMO PAYS gained a second question: no two runs of one widget may be painted on top of each other, read off `scene/text_painted` because a run carries no tag and every other read in this tree is tag-keyed. Measured over all 223 example packages -- 31 carry 71 overlapping pairs, 9 cannot boot headless and are recorded as unmeasured rather than clean -- and the counts are a ratchet in docs/text-smear-budget.tsv. 6 counterfactuals, 6 caught. The running app was driven over the wire to prove the reflow end to end: 1440 -> 1800 with the canvas taking the difference and the fixed panes keeping their widths.

the reported symptom was "sometimes a node presses and sometimes it does not" and the model was innocent: every point of every card in every state already resolved to that card. The failure was the router path -- a tagged node that is not pointer-transparent becomes the hit target, its tag resolves to no External, and the press is dropped in silence. Declared `none`: this is a defect repair and three gates, and no Phase B capability moved. TWO FAMILIES WERE OPAQUE and one of them is a CRATE: every wire on the canvas, whose bounding box is most of the canvas, and the settings form's badges, which every consumer of that painter inherits. Measured by reverting rather than argued: with the wires opaque the application never received the cursor at all, reporting 0,0 after a real warp onto the canvas. THE GUARANTEE MOVED TO WHERE THE NODE IS PAINTED -- the crate now tests that every tag it writes is transparent, because a consumer's suite can only find this one screen at a time and one screen did, from a person clicking on it. THE SWEEPS ARE DERIVED, not sampled: every card presses and drags to ITSELF in every state (the harder question -- after the press, was the thing that moved the thing under the cursor), a 6x6 grid over every card in every state reaches that card, and every tag but the root is transparent at every state. A counterfactual that shortened the first sweep to one card was caught, and one that edited a line the real setting overrode reported PASSED, which is what the driver exists to notice. The real-mouse probe corrects its aim against the application's own reported cursor instead of a once-calibrated window offset -- placement is a per-run fact, and a probe near a card edge was flaky without it; three runs, no flake. ALSO CLEARED, because the push gate demanded it: the catalog axis re-judged 96 -> 97 (round-axis evidence 9 -> 12). The point is R1654's text-overflow arms -- a property every control's label could set and none could rely on, since the eliding arm was declared in R47.5 and implemented by nobody -- and it passes the floor rather than reaching it, because the shortened string is published where the reference cannot report it at all. The axis's own gap list is otherwise untouched and says so: two wheel implementors, four mnemonic sites, one disabled-cascade consumer, four absent widget kinds. One item was ADDED to that list by this round rather than removed -- nothing in the catalogue except this form now tests that the tags it paints are transparent to the router.

scene/containment: a painted mark reports the box it left, per edge, with the string a reader loses; External::on_resize wired (a declared §5.15 arm with zero call sites); the node card's box derived from its rows; window SIZE promoted to an axis in the painted sweep

the SCE pin moves 8597e692 -> 3fecb424 (74 commits) and the policy that came with it is consumed: a forge diagnostic now names the build that emitted it. Declared `none` -- a dependency bump plus a build-tool wire field, and no Phase B capability moved; the RPC surface this would touch (113 methods, none answering which build) is registered as debt rather than credited here. THE MIRROR CLAIM HAD GONE FALSE WITH NOTHING CHANGING IN THIS TREE. pinion-forge's wire module says it mirrors the SCE v1 diagnostic record per schemas/sce-diagnostic.v1.schema.json; upstream made `generator` a REQUIRED field on that schema, so the sentence stopped being true at the moment of the bump and no file here had to be edited for that to happen. The stated reason is the one that generalises: while a wire surface is pre-release a consumer is told to pin a commit rather than trust the schema version, and a consumer cannot follow that instruction unless the payload names the commit it came from. THE CENSUS IS THE PATTERN. The gate destructures a real sce-build diagnostic with no `..`, so every field on SCE's record is either mirrored here or named as deliberately absent with its reason, and a field added upstream fails to COMPILE rather than being absorbed by silence. That is the direction that matters -- the pre-existing wire_record_has_required_fields test hand-listed the required fields and passed the whole time `generator` was missing. The exclusions are argued rather than listed: `spec` and `spec_provenance` are SCXML anchors pinion's closed namespace has no peer for (RFC 001 §4), `expected` and `fix` are SCE's repair-loop payload pinion emits none of, `question_kind` classifies an authoring question where pinion's diagnostics are all refusals. THE STAMP IS A COMMIT, NOT THE VERSION: every pinion crate carries 0.0.1 from the workspace, so two builds a hundred rounds apart report the same string -- build.rs resolves the commit the same way sce-build's does, watching HEAD and packed-refs so it cannot go stale mid-session, and reporting `unknown` on a checkout-less build rather than a claim it cannot keep. 6 counterfactuals, 6 caught, across two gates: four on the record (drop the stamp, stamp the crate version, invent a key outside the mirrored shape, let the nested location object drift col -> column) and two on the pin itself (either SCE rev alone reverted, which is the split-graph failure the dual-pin gate exists to name).

a keystroke says when it ARRIVED, so a binding stops judging the user's timeline against its own workload. Declared `none` -- this is an input-dispatch capability for an embedder, not a widget or a view surface, and no Phase B axis moved. THE CONSUMER'S REQUEST NAMED A TYPE NOTHING DRIVES. It was filed against `pinion_core::event::KeyEvent`; measured, that type has one construction site in the tree, its own test, and no dispatch path reaches it, so satisfying the request as written would have delivered nothing. The report's own prose gets it right two paragraphs later -- nothing on the DISPATCH path exposes a time -- and the dispatch path is `WidgetCore::apply_key` / `apply_key_repeat`. THE DEFECT: the only clock a binding could read was `Instant::now()` inside its own handler, which is when this app got round to the key rather than when the key arrived, later by however long the PREVIOUS handler took -- so any window judged on it shrinks by exactly the work the app is doing. Measured by the consumer at 2x CPU oversubscription: a 500 ms repeat window lost two presses out of three and they went through to the terminal underneath as raw escapes, with their terminal frontend unaffected because its input layer hands over the read a key came out of. TWO HALVES, BOTH NEEDED: an instant and a batch answer different questions and neither derives the other, so `arrived_with` is published as a predicate rather than leaving a consumer to compare ids; a unit test holds the halves apart on purpose, which is what makes swapping the predicate to compare instants a caught counterfactual. THE DELIVERY IS A PROPERTY OF THE LOOP ITERATION, not of a dispatch, so it lives on the shell and each backend says where its handovers begin: winit's `new_events` (before any event of that iteration is dispatched -- that ordering IS the capability), the terminal's "was it already waiting when the previous dispatch returned" (deliberately not "same read", which crossterm does not say and which "already waiting" is the proxy for), and one RPC drain. WHAT IT IS NOT is stated rather than implied: not when the human pressed, because no portable windowing layer offers that -- winit exposes no event timestamp -- so it is stamped as the handover opens, which is the whole of what the defect needs. A struct rather than a fifth parameter, because this entry point already grew once by growing a hook and `KeyPress` being non_exhaustive means the next fact is a field. 5/5 counterfactuals after a first run at 3/5: CF-2 PASSED and it was the finding of the round -- reintroducing the exact defect on the GUI path left the whole suite green, because every test written so far drove `CoreShell` or the RPC drain and neither goes through `ShellCore::apply_key_inner`. Both winit arms now assert for themselves. Also closed by measurement rather than work: two of the four items the handoff lists as open are already delivered, one of them IN the pin the consumer is on.

a consumer that speaks only the JSON-RPC wire links no font stack -- and the fix is not the one that was asked for, because that one does not work. Declared `none`: a dependency-layering repair and a gate, no Phase B capability moved. THE ASK was a feature over the three text dependencies pinion-rpc declares, with the RPC methods that shape text cfg'd out of the catalogue when it is off. TWO CHEAP MEASUREMENTS CHANGED THE ANSWER. Which dependency carries it: `pinion-text-font` depends on `pinion-text-unicode` and nothing else, `pinion-text-unicode` on nothing, and only `pinion-text` reaches parley -- so gating all three would have removed eleven `font/*` methods and the normalisation method to solve a problem none of them cause. How many paths reach it: `cargo tree -i` answers TWO, the direct declaration and again through `pinion-runtime`, which pinion-rpc uses at 101 sites and cannot stop using -- so the fix as proposed leaves the font stack linked and the build still broken. The report's own not-verified section says it never tried the fix; trying it is what finds this. WHAT ACTUALLY MOVES is parley's default `system` feature, which forwards to `fontique/system` and is the sole reason fontconfig's development headers become a build requirement of everything downstream. Declining it at the workspace root and re-enabling it through a `system-fonts` feature that is ON by default gives an external consumer `default-features = false` and changes nothing here. NO METHOD DISAPPEARS, which is the part worth stating: every surface that shapes text compiles and answers in both builds and `rpc/methods` returns the same catalogue, because what the switch moves is which fonts the stack can FIND, not which questions it can be asked -- the proposal would have gated a capability to solve a linking problem. MEASURED AGAINST A REAL EXTERNAL MANIFEST outside this workspace, both directions, because cargo tree inside it unifies other members' features and reports the fix as not working; the wire-only consumer builds with no font stack in the graph. THE GATE IS A CLOSURE over the dependency graph rather than a fact about one manifest -- every path must decline, and a third path is one ordinary-looking Cargo.toml line away -- so `tools/wire_only_deps.py` walks it and pre-push runs its selftest first. DESIGNING THE COUNTERFACTUALS FOUND A HOLE IN THAT GATE BEFORE THEY RAN: the first draft never checked that a crate's switch NAMES the edge it declined, so forwarding to pinion-text and forgetting pinion-runtime would have passed while a default build silently lost system fonts -- the same second path the report missed, arriving again from the opposite direction. 4/4 counterfactuals.

every measurement in this tree shapes against ONE pinned face. Declared none: a determinism repair on the demo harness, no Phase B capability moved. R1656's ink ratchet is a function of the host's font database, so budgets measured on one machine gave a different verdict on CI -- 33 sweep runs red on 8 examples that pass locally. Reproduced with a DejaVu-only fontconfig; three other hypotheses killed first (geometry, a silently-skipped gate, run-to-run flake). The control that misled: remove ALL fonts and there is no ink, so nothing overflows and fonts read as innocent -- CI has different fonts, not none. THE FIRST FIX WAS MEASURED WRONG: an own-fonts LayoutCache made three hosts agree and left the screen with ZERO painted runs, so 0 escapes was green for the wrong reason. Replacing the DATABASE keeps fallback intact and gives it one thing to find. The pinned set is exactly one face and that is load-bearing -- a second face moves LATIN tick labels, because the styles name families neither provides. Not finished: the budgets are stale against the now-reproducible number and CI is still red.

the two ink ratchets get a producer. Declared none: tooling for a determinism repair, no Phase B capability moved. R1656 measured 223 surfaces by hand and left no way to do it again, and BOTH of the failures that followed are downstream of that absence -- when the numbers turned out host-dependent there was nothing to re-run, and when a surface could not be measured there was nowhere to say so. The tool refuses to run with the font pin off, derives its population from the tree rather than listing it, and emits a THIRD state: a surface that could not be measured gets a row saying so with its reason, where before it got no row and no row reads as the strictest budget there is, chosen by nobody. Not finished: the full re-measurement takes hours, the parsers still read the two-state form, and the pin still has no gate.

a pane says what no scrolling can reach. THE TWO DEFECTS THAT MATTER HAD ONE ANSWER: a mark the pane has scrolled past (the reader scrolls back) and a mark nothing can bring into view (the pane does not scroll, or its content extent stops short). Measured on a synthetic pane BEFORE building anything -- the reachable row produced no containment report at all and the unreachable one produced fate "clipped", the same word a two-pixel line-box rounding gets. `pinion_core::reach` derives the missing fact per mark: the innermost enclosing viewport, its content extent, its range, and either the least-move offset that shows it or how far past the reachable box it sits. THE WINDOW IS THAT SAME FUNCTION WITH RANGE (0,0), which is what makes "this pane does not scroll" and "this pane scrolls" two values of one derivation instead of two checks kept in step -- making a pane scrollable MOVES a mark from lost to scrollable, and that move is what a gate can watch. Published as `scene/scroll_reach`. THE REFERENCE WAS PROBED OUT-OF-TREE and has no equivalent: its scroll area derives a live range from the laid-out child (parity, since R55.C here) but overflow can only be INFERRED from a scroll bar maximum, which is also its answer for an area that never set a range -- so a pane that does not scroll is, from outside the widget, indistinguishable from one whose content fits. THE PANE IS A CRATE CAPABILITY: `pinion_widget_paint::pane::scroll_pane` derives the extent from the children handed to it and lowers it as a minimum, so the number a consumer would otherwise keep in step with its own layout does not exist; `PanePointer` is there because a tagged pane the router resolves with no External behind it eats every press (R1655), which adding panes reproduced on two panes at once and the screen's own gate caught. CONSUMERS: the node lab's palette and inspector, and the analysis shell's board -- the two open scroll debts, both closed with gates rather than by hand. THE LARGEST FINDING WAS A COUNTERFACTUAL THAT PASSED: un-scrolling the palette left the new sweep green, because the sweep's smallest swept size was MIN_H, and MIN_H had been set to the panes' CONTENT HEIGHT precisely because they did not scroll. The gate was measuring against a number the defect chose. R1656 wrote that answer down and could not take it; the panes scroll now, so the floor came down 780 -> 360 and the counterfactual goes red with the window named as the viewport whose range is zero. Also: the end-to-end probe drives the PUBLISHED offset and then presses, which found the palette's hit test still answering in unscrolled coordinates -- 33 of 139 published offsets landed on the wrong row.

a decoded field says which bytes it came from. THE CENSUS CLAIMED THIS AND NO SURFACE HELD IT: docs/analyzer-census.json carried capture.t0.3 -- bidirectional highlight between a field and its bytes -- as a `have` covered by widgets::hex_dump plus scene/marks. Driven on the wire before building anything, the dissection External publishes 13 paths and NOT ONE names a byte, and the hex External publishes 17 and NOT ONE names a field: the verdict was covering the byte-to-CELL pair, which is a different pair. That is the error direction R1602 named as the expensive one -- a wrong `have` inflates silently, where a wrong `absent` self-corrects when somebody reaches for it. pinion_core::widgets::field_bytes is the relation: ONE list of FieldSpans, forward extent_of / selection_for (already shaped as the ByteSelection a hex view highlights) and inverse layers_at, with owner_at DEFINED as the last link of that chain rather than computed a second way, because a second traversal is a second chance to disagree. THE MARKS THIS TREE ALREADY HAD ARE NOT THIS, and each gap is asserted against a real MarkSet rather than claimed: one index space so a reassembled payload has no address, overlap as a PAINT rule so a child escaping its parent is accepted and paints something plausible, two answers where there are three (unclaimed and past-the-end are both the empty list), and no arm for a field with no bytes so `computed` and `nobody declared this` are the same answer. The dissection is now the model and ByteMap::marks DERIVES the MarkSet, which is the direction that cannot drift. A SOURCE AND NOT JUST AN OFFSET: a payload reassembled from three fragments is a real field whose bytes are in a different buffer from the frame that carried the last one, so nesting is checked WITHIN a source and a child in another source is how reassembly is expressed rather than a violation. THE REFERENCE FLOOR WAS MEASURED, NOT READ: its mechanism for two views sharing one selection REFUSES two views over different models -- the runtime says so and the byte view keeps its own -- so selecting a field selects zero bytes, and 0 of its 29 selection-model methods and 0 of its 76 item-model methods name a byte extent. CONSUMER: examples/hello-packet-view, the analysis tool's capture viewer assembled against a written-down specification of the reference screen, with the sweep this project now demands -- 8 states x 3 sizes over forward, backward, reachable, contained, disjoint and the round's own law. ITS FIRST RUN FOUND FOUR REAL DEFECTS, all the same shape and all fixed by derivation rather than by moving a number: a list floor picked as a round number that the fixed columns alone exceeded (so the flexible column collapsed and its header stopped being painted), and three places where a fixed slot was given to a run whose length nobody had measured. AXIS RE-JUDGMENT, 86 -> 88, demanded by round-axis going 23 -> 29: folds in the measurement R1644 recorded and deliberately did not spend, re-measured this round rather than copied (DCC 58/76, engine 132/211, node graph 69). This round's OWN work is deliberately not counted, and that is a finding: the axis's artifact list has held row-dissect, hex-dump and inspector for hundreds of rounds while its judgment method measures three families that exclude all three.

a screen says whether a press can reach anything. Filed dcc because the round's forcing consumer is hello-packet-view, this axis's own capture viewer, and it went from a screen on which NO press anywhere in the window did anything to one a mouse drives -- a capability the axis is named for, not a gate. THE REPORT READ CLEAN IN EVERY FIELD. scene/pointer_reach had four, all read off the PAINT tree, and a screen whose widgets are registered under names nothing painted carries reads clean in all four: nothing deliverable because no tag resolves, no shadows because there is no victim to shadow, nothing unreachable because that population IS the tags that resolved. The only trace was `deliverable: 0`, which is byte-identical to the honest answer a screen with no widgets gives -- so the boot gate printed the diagnosis and passed, for a round, while a person pressing the window got nothing. Same collapse R1661 and R1662 fixed in the budget files (no entry vs measured zero), one layer up. THE FIX WALKS THE JOIN FROM THE OTHER SIDE: `externals` pairs every tagged External with the shallowest painted tag that routes to it, so the failure has a NAME, and `is_dead_to_a_pointer` is derived from that list rather than stored beside it. All-and-not-any, because one unrouted widget is ordinary (a model registered for scene/query has no surface) while a roster with none routed is a dead window; and an empty roster is not dead, or `no widgets yet` and `the wiring broke` become one answer again. AND FIXING THE ROUTING LEFT IT DEAF: the router then found the widget, called invoke("send", "PointerDown"), got UnknownPath because the screen had named its action `press`, and dispatch_send DISCARDS that. Registered rather than closed -- 54 files handle `send`, 17 declare it, so the schema cannot judge it and making the refusal fatal breaks the basic catalogue. THE BYPASS NEEDED NO NEW METHOD: scene/click {at} already goes through the router and no sweep had used it; assert_router_press_moves now does, on all three analyzer screens with negative controls. Writing it reproduced its own trap -- geometry read once, pressed five times, the fifth aimed where the fourth had moved the target -- so it takes a tag and resolves the rect at press time. ALSO THE CI SWEEP'S ELEVEN FAILURES, entered as this round's stop-the-line debt and every one a number picked instead of derived: a 24px button holding a 25px line box (now max(WCAG floor, line_box)), a 168px pill holding a 216px label (now content-sized, which then overflowed the WINDOW -- the same defect one level out), a third call site reading a scroll-local rect as a window position, and three demos asserting byte-identity of a framebuffer. That last is a claim about the RASTERISER: ten captures of one unchanged screen are byte-identical on this GPU and differ by 2 to 10 bytes under the software Vulkan CI runs on, every one of them off by exactly 1. So frame equality is judged on per-channel MAGNITUDE against a tolerance the run measures, which is 0 on a deterministic host and therefore byte-identity unchanged.

both vendored pins move together. Declared `none`: a pin bump and its consumption check, no Phase B capability moved. a box owns the border it strokes inside itself, and the ink gate that reports otherwise moves into the framework -- where two of three screens discovered they had never asked it. Filed catalog and the axis re-judged 97 -> 98 as the push gate demanded, the point going to the disabled cascade R1668/R1669 closed rather than to this round's own work. THE RULE: `containment::escapes` compared a mark against its owner's BOX, and a border is ink the box owns inside that box, so a child painted at the owner's full width covered the outline and was reported contained -- CSS has had border box versus content box from the beginning and nothing here expressed the second. R1671 pinned that as a test asserting the WRONG answer with a note saying to rewrite it on the round that fixed it; this is that round. The inset is a match over every `BorderPlacement` rather than a test for one of them, because the first draft asked `is it Inside` and returned the box otherwise, which is right for Outside and WRONG for Center: a centred stroke straddles the edge, so half its width is inside the box and a partially covered pixel is covered, so the inside half rounds up. AND THE PLACEMENT HALF IS PUBLIC, because a caller computing the inset itself is a second copy of the rule free to disagree with the check that reports it. ABSOLUTE PLACEMENT IGNORES PADDING, which is the measurement that made the widget repair a different repair from the one it looked like: the first pass gave `config_form`'s controls a padding equal to their own frame, re-measured, and found the two stepper buttons of every integer row STILL standing on the outline -- the padding had moved the value text and nothing else, because the steppers are placed at PUBLISHED part rectangles and an absolutely-placed child is positioned against its parent's border box. So `lay_parts` lays a shape's affordances in the control's CONTENT rectangle, `control_frame(shape)` says how much that is (two of six shapes put their parts inside a container that strokes `control_skin`), `CONTROL_FRAME` is the width `control_skin` builds its border FROM so the declaration and the paint are one number by construction, and the correspondence is asserted over EVERY arm by reading the border width back out of the painted scene -- a judgement about what a painter does goes wrong silently, and a shape that gained a skin would start painting its own parts over its outline with every test green. In the crate, so every consumer followed. The screen-A allowance that named the two remaining owners is DELETED: an exception mechanism holding the empty set is a place for the next escape to be filed instead of fixed. *** THE ROUND'S REAL FINDING IS A COUNTERFACTUAL THAT PASSED. Screen B holds a byte-identical copy of the ink metric and never called the check with it, and screen C had neither -- so putting screen B's three scrolling panes back over the outlines of the panels holding them was caught by NOTHING, while the same break on screen A was caught immediately. Three mechanical copies of one rule is the immediate-lift case, and the hazard was never the duplication: it was that a metric a screen owns but does not use is a vocabulary the screen cannot speak. `pinion_core::test_fixtures::screen_ink` is that vocabulary -- the stand-in (width font-independent and conservative, height the laid-out line box, because deciding the vertical against a constant makes the gate a fact about the host's fonts), the off-window split, the assertion -- with four negative controls of its own, and all three screens ask. WHAT THE TWO NEW ASKERS FOUND, none of it visible to anything they already ran: screen B's three panes over their panels' outlines, repaired blind by the previous pass and now behind a gate that would have reported them; and on screen C five classes of defect in five different swept states, reported one state at a time because the gate stops at the first -- 32 marks as it opens, then 13, then 9 with a card selected, then 1 with the preset menu open, then 25 with every card shrunk to one cell. Every run placed at an exact rectangle had NO overflow policy, so a label longer than its fixed box was painted past it rather than shortened -- 32 marks including four of the app bar's own, on the one screen of three that never set what screens A and B set on every run. A code chip's word box was wider than the chip at two sites, each from a separately picked inset, which is one rule written twice and got wrong twice. A card reserved only its RESTING outline, so the moment it became the selected one and swapped its 1px outline for the 2px ring, its header and every row of its body stood on the ring's second pixel; the reservation is derived from the two widths now and is deliberately CONSTANT rather than a function of selection, because a content rectangle that changed with the ring would move every row when a person selects a card. And a header too narrow for its own chrome computed a title width with `.max(40)` on the end and measured everything after it from that clamped number, so a card shrunk to one board cell painted `LIVE` 65px past its own frame -- R1668's shape, one fact with two clamps. It gives way in a STATED order now (identity, then the affordance strip dropping from the left so the last-declared stays nearest the edge a hand reaches for, then the ready badge, then the title) and a part that does not fit is not painted; the sweep asserts BOTH sides of that branch, since a give-way that never happens and one that never stops are both invisible to a one-sided check. Moving it is not checkable by itself and that is the trap: the paint and the hit test both read `preset_item_rect`, so changing that function moves BOTH and no assertion comparing them can notice. The shape is pinned against something that is not itself -- the chip: the first row hangs under it, the panel lines up with it, and the menu stays inside the window. AND IT FOUND A THIRD DEFECT ON ITS FIRST RUN, in the arm with no checkbox at all: the LEGEND overflowed the band by two pixels. a box says where its own chrome ends, and every painter in the crate that strokes a border is asked whether it keeps its own contents inside it. Filed catalog. THE GAP WAS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED: a scratchpad probe built against the floor at 6.11 and run offscreen reports that a titled group box there answers `3,23,3,3` for its content margins against a plain framed widget's `2,2,2,2` -- the caption band INCLUDED -- while `containment::content_rect` here subtracted only the border. So the rectangle was parity and the band was a gap, and the scene had no vocabulary in which the question could even be put. `style::Chrome` is that vocabulary: an edge, an extent, and a ROLE from a closed set whose six arms each name a strip something in this tree actually paints. The role is the half the floor cannot carry, and that is measured too rather than argued: probed there, a custom-painted widget publishes the same inset through a four-integer margin setter and reading it back gives four integers with the reason gone, so a caption band and a three pixel border are the same four numbers; and the one place the parts ARE separable is a per-class sub-control enum belonging to about twenty complex controls, which a card header or a dock tab strip is not one of. Here any painter declares a band the same way, and `scene/containment` names what a mark landed on -- `Trespass` is `outside` / `border` / `chrome:<role>`, so "this label is over the title" stops arriving as "this label is out of bounds". THE DECLARATION NEEDED A SECOND HALF AND NEITHER WORKS ALONE: `LayoutStyle::chrome_slot` says a node OCCUPIES its parent's band. Without it, declaring a caption makes every titled frame in the tree report its own title as an escape; without the declaration, whatever is drawn up there is exempt and a label that really did land on the caption goes unreported. With the pair they are two different questions -- content against the content rectangle, chrome against its own band -- and the second is not hypothetical: R1673 found a group box's legend two pixels outside its title band BY ACCIDENT, because nothing was asking. A node claiming a role its parent never reserved is judged as ordinary content rather than exempted, so a typo in a role cannot become a licence. ★★THE CRATE-LEVEL GATE IS THE ROUND'S BULK AND ITS POPULATION IS PARSED, NOT LISTED. R1673 measured fifteen painters in `pinion-widget-paint` calling `with_border` and TWO asking whether their own contents stay inside it; the other thirteen were visible only when a consumer booted, one screen at a time. `frame_gate` is the shared assertion and its census walks this crate's own syntax trees for the two calls -- a border STROKED is production code, a gate RUN is test code, and a regex over the same text cannot tell them apart (R1669's fifth census-over-text failure was exactly that). The direction is `strokes - gated`, so ADDING a bordered painter fails until it asks. There is no exception list and nowhere to put one. ★THE GATE'S FIRST RUN WAS WRONG AND THE WRONGNESS WAS THE FINDING: six painters failed, every one a label overflowing right by 8-60px, and the cause was the gate. `screen_ink`'s stand-in is deliberately wider per character than any real face, which is right for a SCREEN whose boxes are constants an author wrote down and wrong for a WIDGET that sizes its box from its content -- the box had been computed by the real shaper and the check re-measured the same string 60% wider. The ink now comes from the same `LayoutCache` the layout pass shaped with, the arrangement `scene/containment` already uses on the wire, so host font differences move the box and the ink together. What stays caught is the case where they cannot: a box pinned to a constant with a label that outgrows it. ★WHAT THE CORRECTED GATE THEN FOUND, all real, none visible to anything already running: the MENU POPUP stretched its rows across its full width over its own 1px border on both sides, in every dropdown in the tree -- and repairing it revealed a SECOND copy of the popup box in `view_context_menu` with the same defect, which is why the answer is one `popup_box` both builders call rather than two edits. Its clamp is against the OUTER size now, since clamping the content and then growing the box slides the frame back off the edge the clamp exists to keep it on. The DEVTOOLS HIGHLIGHT drew its ring UNDER the node it highlights, on three edges, while its own doc comment promised to leave that node's paint exactly as it was; the placement is `Outside` now, which is what the comment always described, and padding would have been the wrong repair because a devtools overlay that shifts what it inspects is measuring its own effect. The TOOLBAR painted its fifth control 58px past the bar, because CSS's automatic minimum size pins a content-sized flex item at its min-content width however tight the line gets; controls may shrink below their labels now and the labels elide. Six painters declared no overflow policy at all, so `TextOverflow::Visible` painted labels through their own outlines -- R1654 built those arms and no painter here had taken one. ★★THE CHECK MARK IS A PATH, which pays a debt this round's predecessor opened while fixing another: R1673 derived the tick's face from `line_box`, and `line_box` is a RESERVATION generous by ~35% because it must cover a face's ascent, descent and leading. A check mark needs none of those -- it is a shape, not a letter on a baseline -- so the M3 default tick went 18px to 12px and every checkbox in the tree shrank. A polyline has no ascent: it fits by construction, the size token means what it says again, and the commonest glyph in the catalog stops asking the host which fonts it has, which is a direct contribution to zero-flake. The stroke is inset by half its width because a round join reaches exactly that far past the polyline. ★THE ANALYZER CARD IS THE CONSUMER, and its bands are now declared rather than worked out privately: header, and footer in layout-edit mode. The first draft was ONE PIXEL OUT and the containment check found it -- the placement reserves the wider of the two border widths CONSTANTLY so rows do not shift when a card is selected, while the declaration subtracted the border actually drawn. Both sides derive from the same two constants now and a test asserts the identity in all four states, with a negative control, because the consequence is one overhang in one state and the identity holds in all of them. ★★TWO COUNTERFACTUALS PASSED AND BOTH WERE THE SAME CLASS: the wire projection of both new facts had no test. Emptying `trespass` and replacing a band's role with a constant string each left the whole of `pinion-rpc` green -- and that second mutation IS the floor's behaviour, the inset surviving and the reason gone. Both are tested now with negative controls that two facts differing only in their role do not serialize alike. 18/18 counterfactuals caught after those two findings; four were re-authored because their first form did not compile and so tested nothing.

SCE pin bump 60cc4fcb -> 615cb3f6 (19 commits) plus the mirror repair it forced. Declared `none`: a pin bump and its consumption check move no Phase B capability.
