It did, and this is the first bump to exercise the thing R1657 wrote down -- this tree changed nothing and its statement "I mirror the SCE v1 record shape" would have become untrue on its own. The field is classified NOT MIRRORED with its reason and the condition that would reverse it: `expanded_from` names the call site that chose the parameters when a diagnostic's `location` points at a TEMPLATE row rather than the expansion that failed, and is also upstream's signal that the value is synthetic. stop-the-line: the four CI reds are paid off, and the cause of three of them was the demo harness answering a question the framework had already answered better. Declared `none`: a repair round plus one new introspection read, with no axis re-judged against measured evidence, moves no completion number -- `scene/tag_rects` is a new capability but the api axis is judged on method STABILISATION (schemas, versioning, deprecation) and none of that moved. THE RED WAS ONE THING AND NOT WHERE THE PREVIOUS ROUND LOOKED: three data-grid demos scrubbed zero units, and driving it rather than reasoning about it showed the Count cell painted at x=-31 w=100 inside a viewport starting at x=21, so the centre a demo presses is two pixels left of anything, the press is silently dropped, and the RELEASE lands on a different cell and focuses it. ★★THE PREVIOUS ROUND'S REFUTATION WAS WRONG AND THE WAY IT WAS WRONG IS WORTH MORE THAN THE DEFECT: it removed R1673's 1px frame padding, saw the demo still FAIL, and recorded "not the cause, do not chase this again" -- re-run here, with the padding gone the demo dies in its BOOT GATE with a containment error and never reaches the scrub. Two different failures, one verdict, read as one fact. "Still failing" is not "still failing for the same reason". Also measured: even before R1673 that press point sat EXACTLY on the viewport edge, zero pixels of margin, and nothing said so. ★★THE CAUSE IS A MIRROR THAT FOLDS HALF A FACT: `abs_rects_of` re-derives where every tagged mark is painted -- deliberately, because an independent derivation is what makes a focus-ring assertion a comparison rather than a tautology -- and it folded each Scroll's OFFSET and not its CLIP, and let a LATER duplicate tag overwrite an earlier one where the framework keeps the first. `NodeVisit::absolute_rect`'s own doc argues that reported and visible have to be ONE fact because a caller that forgets the second call asserts against a rectangle nothing was drawn in; this was that caller, and nothing had ever checked that the second implementation agreed with the first. ★THE FLOOR MAKES THE SAME SPLIT, measured offscreen at 6.11 rather than argued: its item view answers x=-232 w=99 for the leading column against a 0..368 viewport, its own point-to-item lookup AGREES with that rectangle and names the cell for a point no pointer can occupy, its honest visible-region call is a widget member and an item-view cell is not a widget, and there is no enumeration in either direction. ★`scene/tag_rects` is the enumeration: every intent tag, its own rectangle and the part a pointer reaches, one round trip, `window: null` carried rather than dropped because "no such mark" and "out of sight" take different repairs. Same walk as `bbox_of_tag`, so the single lookup and the enumeration cannot disagree. ★★AND THE TWO QUESTIONS GET TWO NAMES: restoring the clip broke twenty-six demos and the sweep is what said so -- nearly all ask what the VIEW BUILT (which rows a virtualized grid windowed, which cells it asked the model for, that the newest transcript entry is painted BELOW the fold), and a node the renderer clips away is still one the view built. `unclipped_rects_of` is the second name, both readers come out of one walk, and r1445 uses BOTH, one per assertion. `_gate_tag_rects_agree` compares the whole map against the whole enumeration at every demo's boot. ★ONE ASSERTION GOT STRONGER: r1004 claimed "first match revealed at the top" while asserting source row 0 was in the band -- a claim about overdraw. Measured, rows 0-2 are painted above the viewport after that jump; it now asserts the match IS the topmost visible row. ★★THE FOURTH RED WAS A FLAKE BY CONSTRUCTION AND ITS CAUSE IS REMOVABLE: R1664 measured the software rasteriser's one-bit self-disagreement and made assertions tolerate it, with the tolerance sampled from one control pair. Measured here -- ten captures of one unchanged screen, 45 pairs: 3 byte-identical by default, 45 of 45 with the tile count pinned to one. So it is thread interleaving. A control pair agreeing by luck reports a floor of 0 and then fails a tested pair that noised by 1, which is exactly the green-local/red-CI shape; and a tolerance of 1 hides a stale fragment differing by one bit, so removing the noise gives the assertion its strength back. Pinned where the binary is LAUNCHED rather than in the CI job, because a repro on a developer machine has to have the property CI has. ★TWO MORE REDS WERE R1674's: it added `chrome` to the facet census and to the wire and did not move the two demos that restate the key set independently -- which is what those restatements are for, and they fired. The sharper demand was the second: a facet no binding can be seen DECLARING is a key whose presence is untested, and neither binding declared a chrome band, so a third one that does was added. 4/4 counterfactuals caught.

the analyzer's node-graph screen says what it can be asked to DO, and a gate drives every declared way of asking. Filed dcc; no completion re-judged, because the round adds verifiability and two reads rather than a widget. ★★WHY A CENSUS OF THE PAINT COULD NOT FIND THIS: the specification describes panes, roles, cards, fields and a hint strip, and the forward/backward sweep compares the painted scene against all of it -- but an operation the screen does not answer PAINTS NOTHING, so there is no tag to look for and no run to measure. The blind spot is measured rather than estimated: the reference prototype publishes its own operation list and measures its own coverage against it, so the population is ITS declaration, and against those thirty this screen answered seven outright and sixteen not at all while every check here was green. ★★TWO COLUMNS OF CAUSE, BECAUSE THAT IS WHERE THE DEFECTS LIVE: every failure a person reported on this screen had one shape -- the screen advertises an operation, an agent driving the wire gets it, and the pointer does not (a wheel that zooms through an action and not through the wheel hook, a form row whose press resolves to a named target and falls through an unhandled arm, a frame that drags without selecting). One column hides all of them because the column that works is the one a test naturally drives. So an operation declares the ACTION an agent invokes and whether a PERSON has a way in, and the gate drives both -- the second through the screen's own pointer handlers, aimed at rectangles read out of the painted scene, never by writing the state, because a state a test invents can be one no mouse can reach. ★ABSENT IS A ROW, NOT A GAP: an operation with no verb and no gesture is written down, which is what lets it be counted, ratcheted and FALSIFIED -- a row claimed absent that turns out to work fails as loudly as one claimed present that does not. ★★★WHAT THE FIRST RUN FOUND, six of eighteen declared ways causing nothing, split three ways. THREE WERE A SILENCE ON THE WIRE: moving a node, moving a frame and re-parenting between frames each had a gesture and NO OBSERVABLE RESULT -- canvas positions lived only inside the document and frame membership was witnessed by a toast sentence, so an agent driving any of the three could not observe its own drag, and a gesture whose effect cannot be read is indistinguishable from one that did nothing. That is precisely how "the frame drags but does not select" survived. `layout` and `frames` are published reads now, in CANVAS coordinates because that is the question a caller placing or comparing nodes asks, with `scene/tag_rects` answering the window question for the same cards. ONE WAS THE DECLARATION GATE DOING ITS JOB: both new reads answered `UnknownIntrospectPath` first, because since R1637 the schema declaration is a PRECONDITION of dispatch and not a description of it. TWO WERE THE TABLE BEING OPTIMISTIC AND BOTH CORRECTIONS ARE MEASUREMENTS: the integer stepper cannot cause an edit on the opening screen because its field is already at its ceiling, so a driver aimed there clamps; and `validate` has NO pointer path at all -- the verdict is derived, causing it means crossing a bound, the stepper correctly refuses and the text rows have no pointer path, so an agent can close the launch gate and a person cannot. Written down rather than assumed away. ★THE COUNT IS EIGHTEEN AND THE READING THAT MOTIVATED THIS SAID SIXTEEN, kept visible rather than reconciled: that reading was three-way and "partly" is a judgement, this is binary and mechanical, and two rows it called partly answered have neither way in (the configuration export says how many keys there are without exporting them; the launch script does not exist). 4/4 counterfactuals caught -- a declared gesture with no driver, a press that never presses, a witness pointed at a slot its verb cannot move, and a ratchet number drifted from the table.

the settings form gains the mirror `settle` never had, and the analyzer's node-graph screen gains the reset family its reference has and it had none of. Filed catalog: `ConfigForm` is a crate widget, so `revert` / `edited` reach every consumer. ★★THE SHAPE IS MEASURED, NOT REMEMBERED: extracting the reference's markup rather than recalling it settles two things a guess gets wrong -- four of its five reset affordances are wrapped in a CONDITIONAL on a per-scope "has this changed" predicate, so a reset with nothing to put back is not disabled but ABSENT, and the fifth (the view) sits unconditionally beside the zoom controls. That asymmetry is a judgement worth keeping: pan and zoom always have a home, while a graph reset appearing out of nowhere over an untouched screen is an invitation to destroy work. ★★★THE REFERENCE DOES EACH RESET IN ONE LINE BECAUSE OF A STRUCTURAL CHOICE, and seeing it is the round's content: it keeps every edit as an OVERLAY on the opening state, so a reset is one clear and "is there anything to put back" is one is_empty. This tree mutates in place, so both facts are derived by comparing against the SPECIFICATION -- which is where the opening state comes from, so there is no snapshot to fall out of step. The two halves are ONE TYPE (`changed` / `apply`) because a screen deciding for itself when to show a "put it back" affordance is a second author of the rule, and that failure is silent in both directions: a button over an unchanged screen does nothing when pressed, a missing one strands the change. ★★THE SUBSTRATE HAD THE ASYMMETRY WRITTEN INTO IT AND NOBODY HAD NAMED IT: `ConfigField::settle` has existed since R1651 -- accept the current value as the one this form opened with -- and there was no way back. `revert` is its mirror and `edited` is the question it answers. The MEMBERSHIP half is not decoration and a value-only baseline is exactly what this type had: a row ADDED after the form opened is NOT edited (its value is its original) and a row REMOVED is not there to be asked, and both are changes. `opened_with` carries KEYS rather than a copy of the rows, because add and remove only MOVE a field between the held and offered sets so the union is invariant; the opening ORDER is restored too, which a set-based repair loses and which is what a reader navigates a form by. `settle` now accepts the shape as well as the values, because a launch means "what is running now IS what the screen shows". ★★THE GATE LEARNED A REAL PROPERTY OF THE TOOL: R1677's operation gate drives every declared way from a FRESH screen, and a reset cannot be caused from a fresh screen at all -- there is nothing to put back and its affordance is not painted. That is not an awkwardness to route around, it is WHY the reference gates those four buttons. `OperationSpec::needs` names the operation that has to have run first and the gate reaches it the way a person would, by doing the earlier thing and preferring its GESTURE where it has one; a setup that wrote the state directly would let a reset be proven against a state no session can produce. A `needs` naming an operation the table does not hold fails, and one whose target has no way in at all fails too -- an unreachable precondition would silently stop exercising the operation that declared it. ★THE BACKWARD CHECK GREW ONE NEW IDEA: the four conditional affordances are tags that are legitimately absent, so the specification names precisely the buttons that must exist at any given moment rather than declaring a family that may or may not be there. That makes the in-process check unable to see a `changed_scopes` that always answered yes -- the paint and the specification both read it -- and the DEMO is what catches it, asserting from outside that a gated affordance is absent on the opening screen. Measured: the counterfactual that makes every affordance unconditional is caught there and NOWHERE ELSE. ★WHAT DID NOT COME ACROSS, STATED RATHER THAN LEFT TO A DIFF: the reference counts an edit made and then undone as a change because its overlay still holds the key, while a comparison says the screen is back where it started and hides the button -- the button's job is to put something back, so the derived answer is the one kept. And its view reset goes to 100% while this one goes to the zoom the SCREEN specification opens at; "reset" means "back to how it opened" in both and the two files disagree about what that is. `seed_links` lifted out of `opening` because a reset re-authors those links and the accept-pin run arithmetic must not exist twice. `ABSENT_OPERATIONS` 18 -> 13. 4/4 counterfactuals caught.

every debt this session opened is paid, and paying two of them found defects neither debt note knew about. Filed catalog: the repairs land in the settings-form crate and in the analyzer screen's own gates. ★★★THE AFFORDANCE GATE FOUND A REAL DEFECT ON ITS FIRST RUN, WHICH IS WHY IT HAD TO STOP ASKING THE PREDICATE: R1678's counterfactual showed that making `changed_scopes` always answer yes left all thirty-six in-process checks GREEN, because the paint and the specification both derive from that one function and therefore move together. The repair is not a second copy of the predicate -- it is to judge by RESULT: in every swept state, for every gated scope, take the witness, apply the reset, take it again, assert the button was painted IFF the value moved. Nothing in that test knows what the predicate answers. Its first run reported the LINK reset as changing the screen in all eight states including the opening one, where the affordance was correctly absent: the reset cleared every link and re-authored the set, and the model assigns a fresh identifier to each new link, so putting an UNTOUCHED graph back renumbered all seven. The reference's reset is idempotent because it drops an overlay that is already empty; this one now earns it by DIFFING -- removing only what the specification lacks, adding only what is missing, so a link nobody touched keeps its identity. It deliberately does NOT consult `changed`, because an apply that early-returned on "nothing differs" would make the new gate compare the predicate with itself. ★★THE LAYOUT REPAIR WAS UNPROVABLE UNTIL A COUNTERFACTUAL SAID SO, AND THE REASON WAS A SILENT NO-OP: the predicate's population was the specification's node list, so a card the palette added could be dragged anywhere and the screen reported its layout unchanged; it now compares every card against where it CAME INTO BEING, recorded at creation (from the specification for the opening cards, from the placement arithmetic for an added one) because a card the specification does not describe has no other source. The swept states had no state where an added card is dragged -- which the debt note itself had said -- and adding one was not enough: the first draft aimed the drag with `card_rect`, which answers in the WORLD SURFACE's coordinates while `move_cursor` takes the WINDOW's, so the press went nowhere, the state was a no-op, and the counterfactual for the very defect it was written for PASSED. ★AND THAT STATE EXPOSED A STRUCTURAL FACT: the swept states have two consumers with opposite assumptions -- the painted sweeps apply them cumulatively (state n is state n-1 plus one edit) while the operation and affordance gates reset before each, because their rows must be independent. A state leaning on an earlier one for the card it drags passed three tests and panicked in the fourth; it is self-contained now and the reason is written where the next author will be standing. ★THE OTHER TWO ARE TRIPWIRES PUT WHERE THE COST BELONGS: the facet census gains a test beside itself that reads both demos' hand-written restatements and fails when they drift -- those restatements stay hand-written ON PURPOSE, since their job is to fail when the projection and the type drift TOGETHER and a list derived from the wire would agree with the wire by construction, so only the moment of discovery moves, from a CI run to the commit that caused it. And the two rect readers: MEASURED first (25 demos read the placement reader, NONE aims a press with it) then held there by an AST taint check in the harness suite pre-push already runs, because aiming a press with the placement reader re-creates exactly what R1676 paid off. What that check cannot see -- a rect through a parameter or a container -- is stated in it rather than left to be discovered by getting away with it. 5/5 counterfactuals caught, two of them after a first attempt that PASSED or did not compile and taught something either way.

The tempting read is "that is the red I fixed, override and go"; the entry two rounds earlier says why not -- "still failing" is not "still failing for the same reason". The entry plan starts with a PARSER census rather than a grep and names the deeper repair: letting `TextOverflow` see the parent's content box, so "which box is this policy about" becomes the framework's answer instead of each painter's. ★AND THE GATE THAT FOUND IT CANNOT FIND THE REST HERE: `frame_gate` measures with the HOST's fonts, so this whole class stays green locally and turns red elsewhere. The reproduction path exists and is written down; wiring it into a run somebody actually performs is that debt's work, not a claim made here. Verified under BOTH font sets and with `--no-fail-fast`, because cargo's default stops at the first failing test binary and a second font-dependent failure would have been invisible behind this one. ★★AND THE PUSH DEMANDED A RE-JUDGMENT OF THIS AXIS, WHICH HOLDS AT 98 — folded into this round's row rather than declared as its own, because a re-judgment advances no axis (R1604) and this round's row already names the axis it repaired; the number did not move, so nothing credits itself for being looked at. DEMANDED by the tool at the push (round-axis 16 -> 22, +38%). ★HOLDING STILL IS THE HONEST OUTCOME AND THE TOOL ASKS FOR A LOOK, NOT A MOVE: six rounds declared this axis since R1672 and every one added CORRECTNESS to widgets the catalogue already has, not surface it lacks -- a box says where its own chrome ends and all fifteen bordered painters are asked whether they keep their contents inside it (R1674), the check mark became a path so the commonest glyph in the catalogue stopped asking the host which fonts it has, the settings form gained `revert` and `edited` (the mirror `settle` never had, covering values AND rows added or taken away, R1678), and a toolbar label may finally shrink below its own text so the elide policy fires against the box that actually constrains it (R1680). ★★THE NAMED GAPS ARE RE-MEASURED AND UNMOVED, WHICH IS WHAT DECIDES IT: `External::wheel` still has exactly TWO implementors in the widget catalogue -- `slider` and `spin_button`, the same two since R1554 -- so the largest cross-cutting item is where it was, and the analyzer's node canvas hitting it from a consumer screen this session (its hint strip advertises a wheel zoom no wheel answers) is evidence the gap is REAL rather than evidence it shrank. The four absent widget kinds are still four. A round that improves a widget the tree already has creates no artifact, which is why this ledger exists; what it cannot do is turn depth into breadth.

a link's life after it is drawn: the node-graph crate gains an identity-preserving `relink`, and the analyzer's node-graph screen gains delete, re-aim, choose-an-endpoint and adopt. Filed dcc: `Document::relink` is crate surface every node system reaches, and the highest-leverage axis is the one it sits on. ★★★THE VERB IS NOT DISCONNECT-THEN-CONNECT, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS MEASURED: `connect` mints an identifier, so a link taken out and put back is a NEW link and everything holding the old name -- a selection, a breakpoint, an undo entry, a renderer's cache -- is holding a dangling one. This session watched that from the other side one round earlier, when a reset rebuilt its links and silently changed a screen that should not have moved. So the link comes out, the graph is vetted WITHOUT it, and it goes back under its own id, its own mute and its own place in the order; a refusal puts it back exactly as it was and returns the reason intact. The counterfactual that mints a new id is caught by six tests, and the demo catches it end to end. ★★THE FLOOR WAS PROBED RATHER THAN RECALLED, offscreen against the reference toolkit's own relocation verb: a persistent handle SURVIVES an in-place relocation and is INVALIDATED by remove-plus-insert -- which is why that verb exists at all -- but it is offered only over a FLAT sequence, the structural model inherits the base class's `false`, and a refusal carries one bit. A graph is neither a list nor a tree, and "no" is not a reason. ★★AN ENDPOINT BELONGS TO THE LINK, NOT THE NODE, which is the reference's own first sentence about it: a target listening in two places can be dialled two ways, and which one a wire took is a property of the wire. Here that is the accept run's ITEM -- one slot per arriving link, labelled with the address it dials and TYPED by that address's transport -- so choosing an endpoint is the same `relink` over a different socket, and dialling an address this link cannot speak is refused by the model with both transports named. The reference sets an index and checks nothing. ★A COUNTERFACTUAL PASSED AND THE HEADER WAS CORRECTED RATHER THAN THE CODE: lifting the link before the VET rather than merely before the placement is not observable today -- the four vetting rules are provably blind to the link being moved in an acyclic graph, since a cycle through it would have to reach its producing node before arriving at its consuming one. It is the PLACEMENT that can see it, and that is what the failing counterfactual pins. a node's life after it is placed: the node-graph crate gains an identity-preserving rename and a switch that is not a bypass, and the analyzer's node-graph screen gains delete, rename, collapse and switch-off. Filed dcc: `Document::relabel` and `Document::set_disabled` are crate surface every node system reaches, and this is the highest-leverage axis. ★★★A RENAME IS NOT A RE-CREATION, AND THE COST OF PRETENDING OTHERWISE IS MEASURED: the behaviour reference has no rename, so it copies the node under the new name and covers the old one with a deletion -- and then hand-moves TEN side tables to compensate (placement, containment, edits, extra fields, hidden fields, collapse, mute, wire list, selection, draft). Here the node keeps its identifier and the edit moves one string, so the list of things a rename must carry is EMPTY, and that emptiness is the assertion rather than the claim: the form, the placement, the frame, the degree and every link id are compared across the rename. ★★THE FLOOR WAS PROBED OFFSCREEN RATHER THAN RECALLED: against the reference toolkit's own naming surface, an object's identity DOES survive a rename -- but naming a second sibling what the first is called is ACCEPTED, both then hold it, its singular by-name lookup answers an arbitrary one of the two and says nothing, its item model accepts a duplicate display string the same way, and the rename notification carries exactly ONE argument which is the NEW name. So a listener holding a table keyed by the old one is told that something changed and not what to un-key. Two things follow and both are strictly better: a name another node answers to is REFUSED with the holder named, so authored names are unique within a tree and the by-name lookup is a FUNCTION; and the edit ANSWERS the old name, which costs nothing because it was already in hand. Where the invariant is broken from outside the verb -- the field is public -- the singular lookup declines to guess and a plural one says which of the two failures it was, since "nothing answers to this" and "several do" are different problems with different fixes. ★★SWITCHING A NODE OFF IS NOT BYPASSING IT, and the difference is what reaches the nodes downstream: a bypassed node stops computing and its inputs travel straight through, so the graph below carries on; a disabled one produces nothing, so everything that depended on it reads nothing. An editor needs both -- "route around this" and "switch this off" are different intentions -- and a model with only the first makes the second unsayable, which is how it ends up in application state where no derivation can see it. Driven through the evaluator rather than read off the flags, including the one path it could still have leaked through: a disabled source does not hand out its own AUTHORED value either. It deliberately does NOT cascade through containment the way the reference toolkit's enabled-ness cascades through its widget tree, because the relation along which "this is not running" travels in a graph is the FLOW, and the flow cascade is derived rather than authored. ★★THE SCREEN'S SECOND NAME FOR A CARD WAS LIFTED AWAY, AND RENAMING IS WHAT MADE IT LOAD-BEARING: it kept a name-to-node map beside the document's own label, two records of one fact, and a rename updating either alone leaves the canvas and the wire calling one card two things. what leaves the screen: the graph says how it is brought up, and the settings form says what it could not express. It bucketed nodes by "is dialled / dials out" and justified skipping a topological walk with "two peers that dial each other are a legal mesh, so no such order exists". BOTH HALVES WERE FALSE: `connect` refuses a cycle outright, so an authored tree is acyclic by construction and mutual reachability lives in the OBSERVED layer, which is not authored and not deployed. With the excuse gone the bucketing was simply incorrect -- in a chain of four the middle two share a bucket and a NAME decides their order while the links demand the reverse -- and the first fixture was three deep, where the buckets are right by luck. Kahn's walk over the reversed link direction, with the four words kept as the reported REASON a node sits where it does, which is what a reader wants and what the order alone cannot say. ★★A NODE SWITCHED OFF IS NOT STARTED, AND ITS LINKS GO WITH IT -- two claims, and the second is the one a fixture misses: with the middle of a chain off, the two ends never dialled each other, so they are ordered by name and not by a constraint neither of them has. ★★★★★THE SUBSTRATE FINDING IS AN ASYMMETRY THAT HAD BEEN THERE SINCE R1651: the settings form's READ half is total and says so in its own documentation -- `adopt` places every leaf or NAMES it in `Adopted::unplaceable`, "nothing is dropped quietly", because a configuration written by a newer target is the normal case -- and the WRITE half was all-or-nothing. One unparseable row and `document()` hands back an error instead of the other forty rows, which are fine and are what somebody asked for. Invisible while the only caller was a launch gate, because a gate only ever wants the yes-or-no. `ConfigForm::compose` is the total form and `document` is now its NARROWING rather than a second walk, so the pair a caller most needs to trust -- "is this shippable" and "what did not fit" -- cannot disagree. ★★★★★AND A COUNTERFACTUAL PROVED MY OWN SYMMETRY TEST PARTLY VACUOUS: because `document` is DERIVED from `compose`, a `compose` that silently swallowed a defective row moved both sides together -- the row vanishes, `unexpressed` is empty, `complete()` is true, `document` answers Ok, and the two agree on the wrong thing. What caught it was R1651's pre-existing test with a hard-coded expectation. The check now compares the unexpressed rows against `defects()`, which reaches the fields by its own path, and re-running the same counterfactual turns 2 failures into 3. That is the assertion-compared-with-itself class R1681.1, R1682 and R1684.1 each met somewhere else. ★★★THE `unexpressed` POPULATION IS SMALLER THAN THE REFERENCE'S AND THAT IS THE MODEL, NOT A GAP: the reference has two sources -- a value that cannot be encoded, and a row that is not a configuration path at all -- and `ConfigField` is declared with the key BEING the path, verbatim, so there is no second kind of row to fall out. Inventing a table of run-only keys would be inventing the distinction the form was designed without. ★★★★LOOKING AT THE RUNNING SCREEN FOUND A DEFECT NO GATE WAS ASKING ABOUT: the view-reset seat painted `ho…` for `home`. Measured rather than eyeballed -- `scene/text_painted` reports seven shortened runs and six are long sentences elided into bounded strips, which is what that behaviour is for; a control's own NAME is the case where it is a defect. ★★★★★AND THE COUNTERFACTUAL FOR THE GATE THAT REPAIR EARNED WALKED STRAIGHT THROUGH IT: narrowing the seat to prove the check fired did NOT fire it, because the captions were authored as their own constants -- `home` in a 40-wide box on a 34-wide seat, `config` in a 60-wide box on a 66-wide seat inset 12 -- so two of three were painted PAST the button they name, and a caption outside its seat neither elides nor sits inside the rectangle the check asks about. The check went quiet on the worse of the two defects. Captions are derived from the seat now (`seat_caption`), the gate asks BOTH questions -- inside, and not cut -- and generalising it from "is it cut" to "is it inside the control it names" immediately found a third: the zoom readout was painted two pixels inside the `+` button. ★★★THE TOOLBAR'S DECLARED WIDTH WAS A SENTENCE NOBODY READ AND HAD BEEN WRONG SINCE R1678: `TOOLBAR_RIGHT_CLUSTER` said 300 while the view-reset seat R1678 added sits 340 in. That is [[debt-a-stated-limit-is-not-checked-by-anything]] exactly -- a limit in prose is re-derived by whoever is next and the original is never re-read. where the canvas is pointed: framing the whole graph, and going to the first thing wrong with it. The analyser table's LAST two absences, so the count reaches zero for the first time -- and neither was difficult, which is the argument for the column existing: a census of what is ON a screen is blind by construction to what the screen cannot DO, so eleven rounds of green sweeps sat over these two. Filed dcc because what actually landed is node-graph substrate. ★★★★★TWO NODE CANVASES IN THIS TREE HAD WRITTEN THE SAME AFFINE BY HAND: `hello-node-editor` frames its graph by folding a union box, dividing the window by it, clamping into a zoom range and pinning the centre, and `hello-node-lab` was about to write a fourth coordinate conversion of its own to do the same. So `pinion_node_graph::view` is `Camera` (one projection with its own inverse, plus `pinned` -- "put this graph point under this pixel" -- which `zoomed_at` and every viewport write are call shapes of), `ZoomRange` (validated where it is built, so no clamp is ever asked to order two numbers that are not ordered), `Margin` and `Fit`. Both canvases call it; the editor's `frame_all`, its cursor-anchored zoom and both of its projections are now that module, and its own viewport demos are part of this round's gate. ★★★★THE MARGIN DECLARES ITS FRAME OF REFERENCE, WHICH A SINGLE NUMBER CANNOT: `Margin::Canvas` pads the graph's box in graph units so the clearance scales with the diagram, `Margin::Screen` keeps a gutter in pixels so it is the same at every zoom. They produce different scales for one graph, the behaviour canon this tree reproduces uses the first and the DCC "frame selection" idiom uses the second, and both consumers here want the one they want. ★★★A FIT SAYS WHETHER IT FITTED. `Fitted::complete` is false when the zoom floor cannot shrink the graph into the pane -- the one case where the button did not do what it says, and the case the reference toolkit's own fit returns `void` for. ★★★★★AND `card_shape_at` IS WHY THE FIT IS A FUNCTION OF THE GRAPH RATHER THAN OF THE VIEW: a card's box is DERIVED from the zoom it is drawn at (the faces have a legibility floor and the rows collapse below it, both deliberate), so measuring what is on screen and dividing the zoom back out makes "frame the graph" depend on where you were already looking -- press it from two zooms, get two cameras. The scale is a parameter now, the extent is asked at 100%, and the counterfactual that reads the live zoom fails two tests. THE FIRST DRAFT DID EXACTLY THAT FOR THE HOST FRAMES and the idempotence test caught it a pixel at a time. ★★★THE JUMP'S AFFORDANCE IS THE LAUNCH CHIP, which had been on screen saying the verdict and answering no press at all -- the reference's own design, and it cost the toolbar no width, which mattered because the toolbar is what sets this screen's minimum window. `LabState::problems` is the one walk: the panel had been formatting a card's name INTO a sentence and returning the sentence, so "take me to the first one" was unanswerable without parsing the name back out. ★★THE ZOOM PILL IS THE REFERENCE'S NOW -- minus, the read-out, plus, fit -- and the READ-OUT IS THE VIEW RESET, which is what the reference makes it: this screen had a number that could not be pressed beside a seat captioned `home` that the reference does not have. Merging them is one control for one subject and it costs less width than the two did, which is the difference between adding the fit seat and not being able to. ★★★★THE ROSTER: `toolbar_seats` is the ONE list the hit test finds a press in, the accessibility tree names, and the width gate measures. R1687 derived that gate's requirement from rectangles -- a real improvement over the prose it replaced -- but from a list of seven written inside the test, and this round added an eighth seat that list did not have: green, and blind to the very change it was written for. A seat that is not in the roster now fails to COMPILE, because the roster is the only constructor of the toolbar's hits. ★★★★★LOOKING AT THE SCREEN FOUND A CAPABILITY STATED AND UNBUILT FOR THIRTY-SEVEN ROUNDS: four comments in this file say a refusal "has already reached the toast, which is where a person reads it", and there was no toast. `say` wrote a signal, the signal was published on the wire, and nothing painted it -- so every gate was green because every gate reads the wire, while the last card refusing to be deleted and a name already taken were controls that appeared to do nothing. It is painted now, above the hint strip and left of the launch panel, and it does NOT time out: a message that vanishes on a wall clock makes every check that reads it a race, and it is also the complaint people have about toasts. ★★★R1687 LEFT `WIN_W` BELOW `MIN_W` and nothing said so -- the shell was asked to open a window narrower than the minimum handed over in the same call, and every headless probe laid the screen out at a width the screen says it does not support, surviving on two pixels of slack. The design size follows the floor by construction now, asserted at COMPILE time (a runtime check for it is `assert!(true)`, which clippy says and which is the lesson R1644.1 wrote down), and what the tests assert is the pair the shell is actually handed. ★★TWO COUNTERFACTUALS PASSED AND BOTH BECAME TESTS: taking the host frames out of the fit changed nothing observable, because a frame reaches 32 units past its members and the fit pads by 60 -- a silent dependency on one constant exceeding two others -- so the choice is now stated where it can fail, as the fitted box being strictly larger than the cards' own on every side. And swapping the editor's screen margin for a canvas one left every test AND the R877 demo green, because that fit only asserted a zoom BAND; the margin is pinned as what it means now, EXACTLY rather than within a pixel, because the two kinds differ by one pixel here and the first draft's tolerance let the wrong arm through. ★★THAT TEST ALSO SURFACED A PRE-EXISTING LIMIT: `frame_all` cannot centre vertically when the fit wants a negative pan, because a scroll offset floors at zero -- measured at 26 px high, and now an assertion rather than a sentence nobody would read again. ★A SYSTEM-DEPENDENCY DECLARATION WAS MISSING, reported by a consumer building on a clean machine: `sce-build` build-depends on the `libxml` crate, which probes `pkg-config libxml-2.0` and then runs bindgen, so `libxml2-dev` and `libclang-dev` are on the path of every workspace build and were declared nowhere. Invisible because every machine this tree had been built on already had both for other reasons -- a declaration only ever read on machines that satisfy it is a coincidence, not a declaration. 17 counterfactuals, 15 caught outright, 2 passed and turned into the tests above. Measured while repairing it: `scene/set_fps 0` does NOT stop the pan -- with pacing confirming `fps: 0`, one read plus one second of WALL CLOCK plus one read moves the viewport 796 px, which contradicts what that call documents and is registered as its own debt. Reading the ride from the PAINT instead, in one call, then showed excursions of 4-11 px about one run in six, and those were a real tearing defect: `AutoPan::tick` wrote the scroll offset and the dragged nodes as two separate signal writes, so a frame landing between them painted a world that had scrolled and a node that had not followed -- in an editor whose `apply_viewport` already batches for exactly that reason and cites the rule. the analyzer node screen's graph survives being closed, and an archive that will not open says which of four things stopped it. So spec::KEPT is that partition and the gate asks the stronger question: drive each operation, save, open on a screen that has just started, and a SAVED slot must read what it read after while a VOLATILE one must read the opening value. The reference's meter only asks whether a key is classified; a key can be classified as carried and still not come back. ★★THE DISCRIMINATING SET IS CHECKED TOO -- five of the thirty put their scope back to how it opened, so their two readings are equal to begin with and prove nothing about a round trip; every classified slot must therefore have at least one operation that genuinely moves it away from the opening reading. ★★THE COST IS STATED RATHER THAN ABSORBED: the reference puts save/open/clear in the canvas toolbar and so does this, TOOLBAR_RIGHT_CLUSTER 431 to 609 and MIN_W 1447 to 1625, with the number derived by the gate rather than by hand (the hand said 594, and two other gates failed alongside it). ★Violation gained a Display, the one error-shaped type in that crate without one and the one most likely to be put in front of a person.

the palette says how much of the option surface it can author, and every string on that surface has a shape or is named as having none. The behaviour reference publishes FOUR self-censuses; this tree already mirrored its operation table (R1677) and its save partition (R1689), and these are the other two. Filed dcc because the config form IS the property-grid family. ★★★NOTHING DECLARED WHAT THE THING BEING CONFIGURED ACCEPTS, so the two questions a person picking a configuration tool asks first were unanswerable here: a palette of eleven keys over a surface of eleven is finished and over a surface of forty is a start, and the two looked identical. `pinion_core::widgets::config_schema` is the declaration -- leaf paths with the shape each holds, validated where it is built, because a path cannot be a value and a section at once and a schema admitting both would make `document()` pick one silently. Over it, `reached_by` reports TWO numbers (sections 11/19, leaves 11/36) because one hides the other -- a tool can touch every section and reach a small fraction of the leaves, and the sections figure is a FOLD of the leaves figure rather than a second count, since two independently counted numbers over one catalogue can tell different stories -- and `strings` partitions the string half into word-set / has-a-shape / free, exclusive and total BY CONSTRUCTION because the class is read off the declared shape rather than kept in three lists beside it. Neither figure is written anywhere: both are recomputed from the palette every time they are asked, which is the only version of a coverage meter worth painting, and a test drops a field and reads the number to hold that. ★★★★★THE HALF THE REFERENCE DOES NOT HAVE IS THE HALF THAT FOUND THE DEFECT: a reach count answers "is the key offered" and stops, so it is blind to a key offered at a shape the target REFUSES -- the chip is there, the row is there, the typed value is accepted, and the node does not come up, with every count saying that key is covered. `Reach::mistyped` is that column, and this screen had exactly it: the node identifier is read by a parser and was typed as FREE TEXT for its whole life. The repair is not the row -- a row's shape now comes FROM the surface, so the palette cannot offer a key at a shape the target would refuse. ★★★★★AND THE SAME METER WAS FIRST WRITTEN WITH THE WRONG REACH RULE, WHICH A PROOF CAUGHT: it counted a catalogue key on the same root-to-leaf line, which is what a coverage figure over two path lists usually means and is wrong for THIS type -- a form field holds a scalar and `FieldType` has no arm for an object, so a key naming a SECTION composes a string where a subtree belongs. Proven through the form's own composition (the row yields a string at the section's path) and from the other side (the schema refuses to declare a path as both value and section). THREE OF THIS SCREEN'S SIX CHIPS DID EXACTLY THAT -- `timestamping`, `compression`, `plugins` -- and no coverage count could see it, because the key IS on the surface. A leaf is reached only when a catalogue key EQUALS it; the rest are reported as `unauthorable`, kept apart from `unknown` because the two take different repairs. ★★★★THE MIDDLE STRING CLASS NEEDED AN ARM AND `FieldType::Formatted` IS IT, over `TextFormat`: a small declarative grammar (characters with a class and a length, a bounded number, a word from a set, head-sep-tail, a repeated part, an alternation) with no domain in any arm -- an address of the scheme/host:port kind is a composition of three of them, so the next domain needs no new arm. `judge` answers THREE states, and past what a caret-level validator in a mature toolkit answers it says two things that kind of validator does not: `Unfinished` means "some continuation of this would be right", which is what lets a value be TYPED, and every refusal carries the shape as a sentence DERIVED from the declaration plus the byte offset the text first went wrong at. The gate over the third state is a property rather than an example -- every prefix of every acceptable text is never refused, walked over a corpus -- because typing is a walk through prefixes. And because the grammar is data, an agent can read what a field will accept before writing to it. ★★★★★ENFORCING A DECLARED SHAPE FOUND THREE BAD VALUES IN THE SCREEN'S OWN SEED DATA: three of the eight opening identifiers were written as role initials and two of those initials are outside the hexadecimal alphabet the identifier is read with. The fallback was worse than the seed -- every card the palette added opened holding the same unparseable value, so the defect was being PRODUCED once per added node. ★★★★AND THREE EXTRA PROBLEM LINES WERE ENOUGH TO REACH A SECOND DEFECT NOTHING HAD BEEN ABLE TO PRODUCE: the launch gate's panel sized itself from how many problems there are, which is unbounded, so it was placed above the top of the canvas and the pane-local conversion underflowed. It is bounded by the canvas now and COUNTS what it has no room for, because the verdict is derived from all of the problems and a silent truncation leaves a gate closed for reasons the screen is not showing. Driven at the floor window size, where the bound is reachable with a graph a test can build; the first draft guarded that assertion and would have passed on a panel that simply fitted. ★★★TWO COUNTERFACTUALS WERE FINDINGS BEFORE THEY WERE COUNTERFACTUALS: breaking "a number under its minimum can still grow into range" changed NOTHING, because every `Number` this tree builds has min 0 and the branch was unreachable from the corpus -- a bounded number is in the corpus now, which is the fourth occurrence of the class [[debt-a-gate-that-only-sees-correct-code-is-unproven]] names. And the first form of the mistyped break did not COMPILE, which is not a counterfactual. ★★★★★AND ONE COUNTERFACTUAL PASSED, WHICH WAS A THIRD FINDING: replacing the DERIVED sections figure with an independently counted one left everything green, because the two agree on every palette whose keys are all leaves -- they diverge on exactly one shape, a key naming a section, and the test for that case asserted the leaf figure and not the section one. It asserts both now. That is the assertion-in-a-place-it-can-fail lesson met a third time inside one round. 16 counterfactuals: 13 caught in the sweep, the other 3 after the break was made compilable or the assertion it needed was written. ★★★THE KILLED FIRST SWEEP LEFT THE TREE MUTATED AND THE CHECK MISSED IT -- exactly the hazard the driver's own docs record -- and what hid it is that the mutation was behaviourally inert, so the second run's baseline was GREEN over a tree nobody intended. ★★LOOKING AT THE WINDOW RENAMED THE METER: the label said `fields`, sitting directly above a form of field rows whose count happened to equal the section count beside it, so its two plausible readings agreed by coincidence. ★AND THE REFERENCE-MATCH DEMO'S PRESS CENSUS LEARNED THAT A CONTROL BELOW A FOLD IS REACHABLE: it read a missing window rectangle as "painted where a pointer cannot reach", which was true only while every control happened to fit at the design size. And AriaRole::name_required, an exhaustive match so a forty-third role cannot inherit an answer nobody chose, excuses only cell / gridcell / generic: ten cells of one grid are the empty half of an optional column, where a name would be an invention rather than a repair. ★★★THE PROMISE CHECKABLE ONLY FROM BELOW: `layout` says the children speak, and nothing asked. Voice::Hollow is that arm, expressed as Relay::unkept -- every relay mapped once to what a broken promise makes it, with the invariant that a relay is reachable exactly when its unkept form is a defect. ★★★THE GHOST EXEMPTION WAS ONE-DIRECTIONAL: it excused a node something POINTS AT and not one that points at painted ink. Eight of this tree's nine ghosts were exactly that shape and none was a defect; a third anchor is a live region, which owes no rectangle because it comes to the reader. ★★THE SECOND CONSUMER: scene/voice answered every binding since R1691 and one screen ever asked it. Four repaired with a test where the derivation lives; the fifth is a no-op that is now ASSERTED to be one, because it keeps the gate on production's path. ★★★★★AND THE CLOSING AUDIT FOUND THE SWEEP ITSELF HAD A HOLE, WHICH PAID FOR A THIRTY-FIRST DEFECT: 328 demos had been run and SIXTY driving edited examples had not, computed mechanically from the diff rather than remembered. Running them was not a formality -- the gate judges the screen an application BOOTS with, and a todo list boots empty, so no census in this round had ever seen it holding rows. One that restores three rows and a filter did, and it announced a Toggle and a Delete button for every row the active filter HIDES: names a reader can land on and tags scene/invoke will fire, with nothing painted behind them, because the accessibility emitter read the unfiltered signal while the paint read the derived visible list. Repaired at the predicate the type already documents as the one driving the visible list, and the counterfactual fails on the old behaviour. 5 crates + 3 examples green, clippy green, 388 demos run against release binaries (328 + the 60-demo gap sweep).

a screen is a tree a reader can walk: an announced role that promises members and holds none is a lie no per-node check can see. Filed modelview because the mechanism is WAI-ARIA's structural relation over tables, trees, grids and lists, its framework consumers are the data-view builders (grid_table_nodes, grouped_grid_access_nodes, listbox_option_nodes), and the forcing screen is a three-pane capture viewer whose grid, tree and byte grid are all Model/View shapes. ★★★THE QUESTION NO EXISTING CENSUS COULD ASK. R1691 asked whether every painted region has a voice; R1692 asked whether that voice says anything usable. Both are about ONE NODE AT A TIME, and neither can see a node that is perfect on its own terms and structurally a lie: a pane announcing role=table, named, with a rectangle a reader can land on, that holds no row. An assistive technology says "table" and there is nothing to move into. Measured on the reference analysis tool's screen B the day this started: 186 addressable regions, THREE announced nodes, two of which were exactly that. ★★★★★THE FLOOR, BUILT AND RUN, IS STRONGER ON ONE SIDE AND ABSENT ON THE OTHER. Two probes compiled against 6.11.1 and executed offscreen. A model-driven 16x7 item view answers 137 nodes, a table interface reporting sixteen rows and seven columns, and a cell lookup by row and column naming the cell and reporting its own row, column and column header -- which is why this round tags every cell rather than only its rows: tagging rows alone would have been strictly LESS navigable than the thing it is meant to beat. The same view with its model emptied answers the table role, a row count of zero, and NO DIAGNOSTIC; a tree with no items answers the same way. A two-column tree -- exactly screen B's decode pane -- announces a row as TWO SIBLING ITEMS, the value reporting itself expandable like the field it belongs to, leaf rows reporting themselves expanded while reporting they cannot expand, and no hierarchy at all. A custom-painted 72-cell pane answers ONE node, empty-named, with no children. So the floor derives a complete tree for the shapes it owns, nothing for the shapes it does not, and in neither case a verdict about the tree's FORM. ★★★★★EMPTINESS IS DECLARED, NOT INFERRED, AND THAT IS WHAT LETS THE GATE BE BUDGET ZERO. A collection with no members is a real state -- a filter that matched nothing, a capture with no messages -- and a rule refusing it would make that state unrepresentable. So the rule is the one R1691 applied to silence: an empty collection is well-formed WHEN IT SAYS IT IS EMPTY, in ARIA's own extent vocabulary (aria-rowcount / aria-colcount / aria-setsize of zero). "It is legitimately empty" stops being an exception a screen pleads and becomes a declaration the census checks. ★★★★MEASURE FIRST, THEN CHOOSE THE BUDGET. A sweep of all 216 answering surfaces found 12 carrying a violation (13 empty, 44 stray) -- small enough to close in the round that found it, which is the only reason the gate refuses at zero instead of becoming another ratchet. 200 would have forced a ratchet, and a ratchet records defects rather than refusing them. ★★★AND THE RULES WERE WRONG TWICE BEFORE THEY WERE RIGHT, both found by running them over the corpus rather than by reasoning: the first draft gave `radio` a required context and false-flagged a standalone one (WAI-ARIA requires radiogroup->radio and not the reverse -- copying one column of an asymmetric relation into the other INVENTS A RULE), and adding declares_empty took the count from 16 surfaces to 12. THE TWELVE WERE THREE CLASSES AND ONLY ONE WAS EXPECTED: three panels announced `list` and had never built a listitem (they paint prose -- and each had a perfectly good NAME the whole time, which is why a good name is not evidence of a right role); five had trees that stopped short (a header strip owning none of its five column headers and itself inside nothing -- the requirement chain is ARIA saying the tree ended two levels early; a calendar owning its seven headers and thirty-one days DIRECTLY, with no weeks in it, so the shape a sighted reader sees was not the shape a reader was given; a group header row with no cell; a command palette announcing a listbox and never one option); three lists open empty and did not say so. ★★★★THE 3RD-CONSUMER ANSWER WAS THE BUILDER, NOT THE CALL SITES: listbox_option_nodes and grid_table_nodes now state their container's extent, so the fourth consumer is right by construction instead of being repaired. ★★★★★TAGGING THE CELLS EXPOSED A PAINTER DEFECT NOBODY COULD HAVE ASKED ABOUT: at the declared floor, message 6's resource name was painted at ZERO WIDTH -- its two annotations are wider than the whole name column, and the column's floor was a number somebody picked. Same defect and same repair as the comment one level up already recorded (a floor somebody picks can be wrong about the thing it is a floor FOR), now derived at compile time from the widest annotation load the capture holds. A sighted reader had been losing that message's name and no check had ever asked whether the cell was painted, BECAUSE UNTIL THIS ROUND THE CELL HAD NO TAG TO ASK ABOUT. ★★★★★AND "IS INTERPRETED" IS STILL NOT "WORKS", AGAIN: this screen matched the chords `Down` and `Up`, which no key press produces -- the shell spells a named key the way the web platform does, and every other example in the tree matches ArrowDown. Its keyboard navigation had never worked from a keyboard, and every test that drove it passed because every test used the screen's own spelling: the test and the defect were the same mistake. The round that announced this list as a `grid` -- a composite widget whose contract IS that the arrows move the selection -- is what made anyone drive a real key. Class measured across all 225 examples: one instance, now zero. Screen B closes at 291 addressable regions, 266 announced, 25 declared quiet, 0 unclassified, 0 voice defects, 276 announced nodes, judged 276, 0 empty, 0 stray -- from 186 regions and 3 nodes. Its spec::Population also settled debt-a-voice-family-can-only-expand-from-a-table-the-spec-has by being the second consumer the debt said was the only possible evidence: it declares a PRODUCT of two tables, a RANGE from a scalar, and four families expanded by a predicate, with no new machinery -- what has to generalise is the expander, which was already a function.

a locked seat is heard, or it is not a locked seat. Filed modelview because the framework deliverable is the shared item-view grid builder, and because the tool DEMANDED this axis's re-judgment (round ledger 11 -> 14, +27%): re-audited, it HOLDS at 95, since all eight gaps R1563 named still stand and what this round closed was never counted. ★★★★★THE SCREEN'S SUBJECT WAS INAUDIBLE. The reference dashboard's point is what the release does NOT have yet -- four widgets placed and NINE RESERVED, each shown rather than hidden and each naming the requirement it is booked under. The framework has computed that reason since R1668 (a kind, a detail, and a recourse derived from the kind, resolved down the subtree by the disabled cascade and published on scene/disabled) and measured the day this started, all ELEVEN locked regions published a complete reason and NOT ONE WAS IN THE ACCESSIBILITY TREE. The screen painted 128 addressable regions, announced FIVE, and scene/conform judged ZERO nodes -- not zero faults, zero JUDGED, because no announced role on it carried a structural requirement at all. ★★★★★THE FLOOR, BUILT AND RUN AT 6.11.1, IS WORSE THAN ONE BIT: a locked list entry answers `focusable, selectable` and carries NO unavailable state at all -- measured in BOTH spellings, the convenience item and a model whose flags() drops the enabled bit -- and so does a locked TAB. A locked plain widget DOES carry the bit, which is how the probe is known sound: the loss belongs to COLLECTIONS, which is exactly what a palette and a navigation rail are, so a reader there is invited to activate the seats the screen has closed. Its section headings come back as list items indistinguishable in role from the entries (sixteen flat items, no grouping, and "thirteen entries, nine reserved" not derivable from anything announced), and the one slot that could carry a reason is free-form prose that on a toolbar action DEFAULTS TO THE ACTION'S OWN LABEL -- measured directly: every unlocked seat's description equals its name. ★★★★MEASURE FIRST, THEN CHOOSE THE BUDGET, again: over 215 answering surfaces there are 13 stated reasons and ELEVEN WERE UNHEARD, all on this one screen, so the gate's new half refuses at ZERO with an empty exception list instead of becoming a ratchet. Two failure shapes, because the repairs differ -- no node at all (announce it) and announced-with-the-reason-dropped (look at the assembler). ★★★★★AND THE ROUND FOUND A RULE LIVING IN PROSE. Two screens hand-rolled a header-row grid and DISAGREED about where the header row sits. WAI-ARIA counts it in aria-rowcount so it must be counted in aria-rowindex -- and grid_table_nodes stated a grid's EXTENT and gave no row or cell its COORDINATES AT ALL, which is below the floor on the dimension the floor is strongest on (its cell query answers the cell's name, its row, its column and its column header). The capture screen's copy numbered its data rows from one, leaving its header unplaced and its last row unreachable. The rule now lives once in the builder, with the row's WAI-ARIA name-from-contents beside it, and BOTH screens were converted onto the builder rather than corrected in place. ★★★THE REASON IS DECLARED ONCE: nothing in the screen's accessibility code restates a lock -- the row declares Unavailable on its layout style and the assembler relays what the cascade resolved -- and a unit test asserts the tree built in isolation carries NO reason at all, so the relay is what the demo proves end to end. ★★THE VOICE CENSUS FOUND ITS OWN as soon as the cells were tagged: the identifier map's unresolved timestamp is painted as an em dash, the typographic stand-in for a value nobody has, and announced as itself it is a punctuation mark with no word in it; it now announces its meaning. ★★★★★AND THE ENTRY CENSUS FOUND R1693's OWN RED: hello-lazy-tree failed the structural gate at boot with a tree holding no treeitem, which is not FORGOTTEN but WAITING -- aria-busy, read from the same predicate the status band already puts into words (R1693.1, committed separately, with a test that fails both ways). A second failure on that demo was proven PRE-EXISTING by running the pristine binary with the gate disabled and comparing the failure MESSAGE. ★★★AND THE THIRD-CONSUMER RULE FIRED: two screens had byte-identical `tagged_label` helpers and this round's table cells made three, so `pinion_widget_paint::run::text_run` is the lift -- holding two decisions in one place, that a run's layout rectangle IS its text rectangle (or every tag-keyed check reads a box the glyphs are not in) and that a run is transparent to the pointer (or it shadows the control it labels). Screen C closes at 193 regions, 190 announced, 3 declared quiet, 0 undecided, 0 voice defects, 159 nodes judged, 0 empty, 0 stray -- from 128 regions and 5 nodes. 14 of 14 counterfactuals CAUGHT, none passed; three were rewritten first because the break did not COMPILE, which tests nothing, and each was recast as a WRONG answer rather than an absent one.

arriving is not highlighting: a navigation rail that moves a string is not a rail that takes you anywhere, and nothing in this tree could tell the two apart. Filed catalog and the axis RE-JUDGED 98 -> 99, which the standing note above demanded be breadth rather than depth: the four absent widget kinds are three, because pinion_core::widgets::destination plus pinion_widget_paint::pages IS the paged container that list has named since R1554. The other three and the wheel hook are untouched, which is why it is one point. ★★★★★THE DEFECT, MEASURED BY DRIVING THE RUNNING APPLICATION THROUGH THE ROUTER BEFORE ANYTHING WAS CHANGED. The analysis tool's dashboard offers seven destinations. Pressing Stream, Decode, Catalog or Settings moved `nav` -- the string the rail highlights ITSELF from, read by nothing else -- and left the painted scene at 193 TAGGED REGIONS BEFORE AND 193 AFTER, nothing added and nothing removed. The screen said Stream and showed the dashboard. On the sibling screen every seat answered "X is not this screen", INCLUDING the seat that screen already was (false) and the two declared unavailable with a stated reason (which got that sentence instead of their reason). And the two screens' rosters share TWO KEYS OUT OF SEVEN: one tool, two lists of what the tool contains. ★★★★★WHY EVERY GATE WAS GREEN THROUGH ALL OF IT: the existing check is assert_router_press_moves, which asserts a press MOVED THE STATE -- exactly what a screen that highlights a seat and shows nothing new does. Moved is not arrived, and the difference is a rectangle. ★★★★THE FLOOR, BUILT AND RUN AT 6.11.1 rather than read about: its paged container addresses a page by ORDINAL; setCurrentIndex returns void so an out-of-range ordinal is a silent no-op with no diagnostic; a DISABLED PAGE IS ARRIVED AT ANYWAY (currentIndex becomes 2 for a page that refuses); a destination that has no page yet cannot be expressed at all; a non-current page stays LIVE and, sent a press, a key and a wheel directly, counted all three -- so input scoping there is a guard the author repeats at every handler, which is precisely what the behaviour reference does (its wheel handler opens by testing that the active section is its own); and the container's accessible value is EMPTY, so no client can ask which page is showing, while a locked rail seat answers focusable, selectable with no unavailable state at all. ★★★★THE SUBSTRATE ANSWERS EACH ROW: the key is the address (an ordinal makes reordering the rail and changing where a press goes the same edit); navigate returns a typed Detour carrying the reason; a destination with no page is an ordinary roster entry whose Standing is Closed; the page that is not current is NEVER CONSTRUCTED, because view_page_region hands the builder only the destination it is at, so scoping is structural rather than remembered; and the region is a named `region` landmark publishing which destination arrived. The reason value is the framework's existing Unavailable rather than a second vocabulary -- one arm added to it, Elsewhere, because a product with more than one surface must be able to say BUILT, SHIPPING AND NOT HERE, and neither reserved (wait for a release that has already arrived) nor unsupported (give up on a feature one window away) means that. It derives its own Recourse::OpenElsewhere, which is the rule that module states for spending an arm: the reader's next action is its own. ★★★A SECOND PAGE, BECAUSE A PAGED REGION WITH ONE PAGE PROVES NOTHING ABOUT PAGING. The reference's own Settings section, reproduced: four switch rows in two groups with the reference's alternating opening values, two affordances booked for a later release, and a two-way appearance segment. Both new control shapes are CATALOGUE WIDGETS rather than hand-drawn -- the first draft painted a box with a word in it and the words sat flush against their left borders, measured by ink span (Import... inked at 683 in a box from 682), and the repair is view_button, which centres with flex. ★★★★★THE CENSUS LEARNED TO WALK MORE THAN ONE SCREEN, which is half of debt-the-voice-gate-judges-only-the-opening-screen and the half that was called unclosable because nothing enumerated the screens an application has. The rail's roster IS that enumeration: every VoiceSpec / SILENCES / LOCKED row now says which destination owns it, the gates drive each open destination and compare in BOTH directions, and a page added without a row fails rather than escaping. Locked regions on this screen went 11 -> 16 as a direct consequence. ★★★★★16 COUNTERFACTUALS, 15 CAUGHT AND THE ONE THAT PASSED IS THE FINDING: emitting the settings page's accessibility nodes while the dashboard is showing left every check green, because they all read the PAINTED scene and a tree can announce what nothing paints. The demo's boot census caught it as four ghosts -- the right answer arriving one build later and only for the destination the application happens to open at -- so the law is now asked of the tree too, in-process, per destination. Two more findings arrived as ordinary failures: the region swallowed every press on its page until pointer transparency became structural in the substrate (the screen's own R1649 gate went red on the first run), and a `part_of` silence pointing at PROSE instead of a tag produced seven dangling rows. Also repaired, this round's defect in miniature: the Add Widget button moved the rail's highlight to a destination the window had not taken anyone to. 4 crates green (317 a11y, 3512 core, 886 widget-paint, 52 shell), 4 analyzer demos green, and the settings page was LOOKED AT -- which is what found the left-flush labels that no value check on this screen could report.

the screen has a keyboard. Declared `none`: this is a STOP-THE-LINE REPAYMENT of the red R1695's push inherited, plus the local gate that should have caught it and did not exist, and no Phase B capability moved -- the axis the repair lands on is accessibility, and R1581 set the precedent that an accessibility repair is not an advance. ★★★★★WHAT WAS RED, AND WHY THE ROUND THAT CAUSED IT COULD NOT SEE IT: two demos, one cause -- `hello-analyzer-shell` presents an interactive ARIA role and `focus/next` from cold answered NOTHING. It announces a navigation landmark of links, two toolbars, a list of items, four tabs, a textbox and thirty-nine buttons, and a keyboard reached none of them. R1694 is what put it there: an interactive role is what enrols a binding in `r1570.1`'s DERIVED population, so the screen joined the gate the moment it started declaring -- and both gates that walk it are python demos that run only in CI. The sibling screen learned the identical lesson at R1693 from the identical pair, which is the part worth keeping: a round that gives a screen its first accessibility tree acquires two gates it has never run. ★★★★THE REPAIR IS THE WAI-ARIA COMPOSITE PATTERN, the shape the sibling already holds: one stop per composite -- application bar, rail, layout bar, board, palette -- rather than one per control, plus the Settings page's switches and appearance segment, which are not inside a composite and declare their own stop through the catalogue widgets. The ring is `spec::FOCUS_RING`, a DECLARATION the paint reads rather than five independent decisions, and each row also says WHAT the stop holds, which is the part a tag cannot carry: an agent reading `focus_ring` off the wire learns that landing on the rail puts it among the tool's destinations rather than on one of them. ★★★★★THE ORDER IS THE PAINT ORDER AND THAT IS RATIFIED, NOT MISSING. The ring starts at the page, because the page must be painted UNDER the chrome, which is not the order a reader would choose. §5.39's own alternatives REJECT a manual tab index -- imitating HTML's tabindex violates the declarative spirit of a view function, automatic traversal is canonical -- so this was NOT worked around. Measured against the floor by building a probe and running it: `setTabOrder(bar,rail)` reorders the chain while the geometry stays put (page y=11, bar y=43, rail y=75 unchanged), so on this dimension the floor is above us, while its API is a static pairwise mutation with no way to ASK a widget its rank where this project publishes the whole enumeration -- each side holds half. Filed as a SPEC ROUND with the argument it has to weigh: "tree order is canonical" is a claim about an order the author CHOSE, and z-order takes that choice away from a screen whose chrome is painted over its page. The debt also records the alternative that needs no tab index at all -- give chrome a layer so child order stops carrying z-order -- and warns against the consumer-side "fix", which puts the chrome underneath the page. ★★★THE LIFT: R1693 wrote a four-line free function to make a painted region a Tab stop and this round needed a verbatim copy on the second screen, which is the exact trigger `Scene::silenced` was lifted on in that same round. It is `Scene::with_focusable` now and the free function is gone. ★★★★AND THE SIBLING SCREEN GAINS THE GATE IT NEVER HAD: a counterfactual reverting the lifted builder left EVERY test in `hello-packet-view` green while that screen lost its whole keyboard -- R1693 added its ring and left it verified only by the slow tree-wide demos. Both screens now assert their own ring in-process, derived from their own specification tables. ★★★THE GATE'S OWN HALF-VACUITY IS CLOSED EXPLICITLY: the paint reads the ring table, so "every declared stop is focusable" compares the table with itself, which R1669's rule says is not a check. What the table cannot produce is a stop it never named, so the enumerated set is closed against the table plus the catalogue widgets -- and the ORDER comparison is discriminating on its own, because paint order is not derived from the table. 5 counterfactuals, 4 caught, and the one that PASSED is a finding: flipping the booked affordance's `focusable` to true changed nothing in the Rust gate OR in the demo's negative control, because the row declares Unavailable and R1554's enumeration returns at a disabled region before reading any child's flag. Nothing was missing -- that rule is tested where it lives -- but a comment was claiming credit for a guarantee it does not provide, and now says which one is load-bearing. Both red gates re-run here against release binaries: r1570.1 151 assertions, r1518 529 assertions over 96 stops in 96 bindings. Five screenshots, one per stop, confirm the overlay ring draws correctly including on the two edge panels where a clipped ring would have been the obvious failure. What this round did NOT do is stated: arrow roving WITHIN each composite, which both analyzer screens lack equally, so it is one shared axis rather than a divergence.
